AD.name: Andorra
AD.headline: Illegal; fines for use, prison for dealing; no medical program
AD.law: Possession, use, cultivation and sale of cannabis are illegal in Andorra. No medical program; a medical-cannabis research study began in 2021.
AD.punishment: Use/possession: fines (reported up to €600 for public use; some sources cite up to €1,200 and short jail). Trafficking: prison (reported up to 2 years for minor cases, more if serious) plus fines.
AD.medical: None yet; government drafting a medicinal-cannabis cultivation bill (single licensed indoor operator, THC under 2%, no recreational use), announced Sept 2026

AE.name: United Arab Emirates
AE.headline: Illegal; zero tolerance; courts have sentenced hashish traffickers to death
AE.law: All use and possession banned under Federal Decree-Law 30 of 2021 (amended 2023). Traces in blood/urine count as use.
AE.punishment: Use: at least 3 months' prison or AED 20,000-100,000 fine (1st offence), more if repeated; foreigners deported. Trafficking: death or life; 3+ on drug death row, no 2025 drug death sentences (HRI).
AE.tourists: No. Travellers testing positive or carrying residue are arrested; fines/deportation.
AE.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: 2012: Abu Dhabi court sentenced 3 Asian men to death for trafficking 53 kg hashish bound for Saudi Arabia; Dubai 2012 Briton Nathaniel Lees + Syrian sentenced to death for 20 g marijuana (later commuted). Death or life for trafficking/import under Decree-Law 30/2021; 3+ on drug death row, no executions reported recently (HRI).

AF.name: Afghanistan
AF.headline: Totally banned under the Taliban; offenders jailed and publicly flogged
AF.law: All cultivation, use, sale and trade of narcotics, incl. cannabis/hashish, banned by Taliban decree (April 2022). Earlier counter-narcotics laws also criminalised cannabis. Enforcement under the Taliban's reading of Sharia.
AF.punishment: Taliban courts hand down prison terms of months to several years plus public flogging (often 10-39 lashes) for hashish and other drug offences, incl. dealing. UN counted 1,100+ people flogged in 2025.
AF.access: No legal access. Hashish is widely produced illicitly, but there is no lawful channel of any kind.
AF.tourists: No. Foreigners face the same Taliban courts.
AF.death_detail: Not a drug death-penalty state per HRI 2025; corporal punishment (flogging) is used instead.

AG.name: Antigua and Barbuda
AG.headline: Up to 15 g and 4 plants allowed in private; Rastafari sacrament legal
AG.law: Misuse of Drugs (Amendment) Act 2018: possessing 15 g or less is not an offence if not smoked in public; households may grow 4 plants. Sale stays illegal. Rastafari may grow and use as sacrament under 2018/2022 laws.
AG.punishment: Up to 15 g in private: no penalty. Smoking in public: warning, then $500 ticket, then $1,500 fine. Above 15 g or any sale: criminal charges with fines and prison.
AG.access: Home grow (4 plants/household) only; no licensed shops. Medical framework planned but not confirmed operating.
AG.tourists: Can possess up to 15 g privately; no legal place to buy.
AG.medical: Medical framework proposed (Cannabis Act); operating status unconfirmed

AL.name: Albania
AL.headline: Illegal for adults; 2023 law allows only licensed medical cultivation for export
AL.law: July 2023 law permits licensed medical and industrial cannabis cultivation, mainly for export; no domestic patient access and few if any licences issued. Recreational possession, cultivation and sale remain crimes.
AL.punishment: Personal possession: criminal; a single personal dose may escape prosecution. Production or trafficking: 5-10 yrs; up to 15+ yrs if organised.
AL.access: No legal access. No domestic medical program.
AL.medical: Export-only production law (2023); no patient program

AM.name: Armenia
AM.headline: Illegal; small amounts fined, licensed industrial hemp allowed
AM.law: Cannabis is banned for recreational and medical use. Small personal amounts are an administrative offence; larger amounts are criminal under the 2022 Criminal Code. Since 2021 licensed companies may handle hemp under 0.3% THC.
AM.punishment: Small amounts: administrative fine. Larger possession: about 1-4 yrs prison. Trafficking/sale: longer prison terms rising with quantity.
AM.access: No recreational or medical access. Only licensed companies may produce/import industrial hemp (≤0.3% THC).
AM.medical: No medical cannabis program; government denies legalisation plans.

AO.name: Angola
AO.headline: Illegal; prison for trafficking, treatment option for users
AO.law: Law 3/99 on drug trafficking and consumption (alongside the 2020 Penal Code) makes using, possessing, growing and selling cannabis (liamba) crimes. Users' sentences can be suspended on condition of treatment.
AO.punishment: Use: short prison terms or fines, which can be suspended with treatment. Trafficking: Supreme Court cases show 5-8 years' prisão maior (52 kg case: 5 years).
AO.access: No legal access. No medical program.
AO.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.

AR.name: Argentina
AR.headline: Private personal use protected by courts; registered medical home grow
AR.law: Law 23.737 still criminalizes possession, but the Supreme Court's Arriola ruling (2009) held private adult use that harms no one is protected, so such cases are dismissed. Medical: Law 27.350 (2017) and REPROCANN registry, overhauled by Res. 1780/2025.
AR.punishment: Personal-use possession: on paper 1 month-2 years (often diverted/dismissed per Arriola). Other possession: 1-6 years. Trafficking/sale (Art. 5): 4-15 years prison.
AR.access: No shops. REPROCANN-registered patients (with a doctor's sign-off) may grow at home or via a grower/association; pharmacy products. 2025 rules shortened permits and tightened requirements.
AR.tourists: No legal purchase; REPROCANN is for residents.
AR.home_grow: Registered patients only (REPROCANN; 9 flowering plants under 2021 rules)
AR.medical: Legal since 2017; REPROCANN registry, tightened in May 2025

AT.name: Austria
AT.headline: Illegal; small personal cases go to health authorities, not court; medical by prescription
AT.law: Possession, cultivation for drug use, and sale are crimes under the Narcotic Substances Act (SMG). For small personal amounts, prosecutors must suspend the case (probation, health-authority referral). Low-THC CBD/hemp products are legal.
AT.punishment: Possession: up to 1 year (6 months if purely personal), normally withdrawn with probation for small amounts. Trafficking: up to 5 years; large quantities 1-15 years.
AT.access: No recreational access. Medical: dronabinol and Sativex on prescription (reimbursement case by case); cannabis flower not prescribable.
AT.home_grow: Illegal (growing to produce THC is a crime)
AT.medical: Dronabinol and Sativex by prescription; no flower

AU.name: Australia
AU.headline: Medical cannabis widely prescribed; recreational illegal except ACT home use
AU.law: Recreational use, possession and sale are illegal under federal and state law. Medicinal cannabis legal federally since 2016 via TGA schemes. ACT legalised small personal possession and home grow for adults in 2020 (sale still illegal).
AU.punishment: Small possession: usually caution, diversion or fine; up to 2 yrs jail possible in some states (e.g. NSW). Trafficking/supply: years in prison; commercial quantities up to life under federal and state law.
AU.access: Very accessible: doctors prescribe via TGA Authorised Prescriber/SAS-B, many telehealth clinics, dispensed at pharmacies. ACT adults may grow 2 plants (4 per household). No legal retail sales.
AU.tourists: No legal purchase; medical use needs an Australian prescription. ACT possession rules apply to all.
AU.possession_limit: ACT: 50 g dried / 150 g wet; illegal elsewhere (small-amount schemes vary)
AU.home_grow: ACT only: 2 plants per adult, max 4 per household; illegal elsewhere
AU.medical: Legal nationally since 2016; TGA-regulated prescriptions, very widely used
AU.subnational: ACT: legal personal use/grow. SA, NT: fines (expiation). WA: Cannabis Intervention Requirement. QLD: 2026 reform: one diversion, then fines.

AZ.name: Azerbaijan
AZ.headline: Illegal; possession beyond tiny amounts is a crime
AZ.law: Criminal Code art. 234 bans possession, cultivation and sale of cannabis. Small amounts for personal use fall under administrative law; amounts above that are criminal.
AZ.punishment: Small amounts: administrative fine or short detention. Possession above small amount: up to about 3 yrs. Trafficking/sale: multi-year prison terms (up to about 12 yrs).

BA.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
BA.headline: Medical use allowed on paper since Dec 2025, not yet working; otherwise illegal
BA.law: Council of Ministers moved cannabis to the strictly controlled list on 29 Dec 2025, allowing authorised pharmaceutical products on prescription. Entity rules still pending (Jul 2026). Recreational use, sale and cultivation illegal.
BA.punishment: Possession for personal use: fine or short prison term depending on entity law. Production and trafficking: criminal, typically 1-10 yrs, more if organised.
BA.access: No practical access yet: medical prescriptions await entity-level regulations. No shops, clubs or home grow.
BA.medical: Legalised Dec 2025 (prescription pharma products only); implementation stalled
BA.subnational: Penalties for possession are set by entity laws (Federation BiH, Republika Srpska, Brcko) and differ.

BB.name: Barbados
BB.headline: Up to 14 g is a $200 ticket; licensed medical dispensaries; Rastafari sacrament
BB.law: Drug Abuse (Prevention and Control) (Amendment) Act 2021: 14 g or less = fixed-penalty ticket, no court or record. Medicinal Cannabis Industry Act 2019 licenses medical use; Sacramental Cannabis Act 2019 permits registered Rastafari use. Recreational sale illegal.
BB.punishment: Up to 14 g: BBD$200 fixed penalty (pay within 30 days). Over 14 g, cultivation or supply: criminal charges with heavy fines and long prison terms for trafficking.
BB.access: Moderate: medical cannabis via prescription at licensed dispensaries (Barbados Medicinal Cannabis Licensing Authority); first licensed therapeutics facility opened 2025.
BB.tourists: No recreational purchase; medical only with prescription.

BD.name: Bangladesh
BD.headline: Illegal; the law allows death for trafficking, but no death sentence for marijuana is documented
BD.law: Narcotics Control Act 2018 (replaced 1990 Act) bans cannabis cultivation, possession, sale and use. Ganja penalties are set by weight and plant count. A 2026 amendment added death for drug dealing via online/digital platforms.
BD.punishment: Ganja (s.36 item 19): up to 5 kg 6 months-5 yrs + fine; 5-15 kg 5-7 yrs; over 15 kg 7-10 yrs. Cultivation (item 18): 1-10 yrs by plant count. Hashish/charas/cannabis resin (class Ka item 7): up to 500 g 1-5 yrs; 500 g-5 kg 5-10 yrs; over 5 kg 10 yrs-life. Online/digital dealing in any narcotic: up to death (s.36A, 2026).
BD.access: No legal access. Historic government ganja shops were closed decades ago.
BD.death_detail: Death (maximum) for dealing any narcotic, incl. ganja, via digital/online means (s.36A, added by Act 101 of 2026). Offline: ganja max 10 yrs; hashish/charas over 5 kg 10 yrs-life (s.36 table items 13-14, 18-19).

BE.name: Belgium
BE.headline: Still illegal, but small adult possession (3 g / 1 plant) is low priority
BE.law: Cannabis remains illegal under the 1921 drugs law. A 2003 law and prosecution guidelines make adult possession of up to 3 g or 1 plant, with no aggravating factors, the lowest priority: a simplified police report, usually no prosecution.
BE.punishment: Possession (small, adult): usually a report or fine; repeat offences can bring higher fines and up to 1 year. Dealing/trafficking: 3 months to 5 years plus fines; up to 15-20 years if aggravated.
BE.access: No recreational access or shops. Medical: only authorised cannabis medicines (e.g. Sativex) on prescription; no flower program. CBD sales allowed under strict rules.
BE.tourists: No legal purchase; tolerance does not cover public nuisance or minors.
BE.medical: Limited: approved cannabinoid medicines (Sativex) by prescription
BE.subnational: Antwerp and Brussels enforce more strictly (immediate fines for any possession).

BF.name: Burkina Faso
BF.headline: Illegal; use and trafficking are criminal
BF.law: Drug-control law (Law 017-2017/AN) bans cultivation, possession, use and trafficking of cannabis. No medical or hemp program.
BF.punishment: Use/possession: prison and/or fines. Trafficking: multi-year prison terms and heavy fines. Exact current ranges not verified.
BF.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
BF.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

BG.name: Bulgaria
BG.headline: Fully illegal, no medical program; possession can bring 1-6 years
BG.law: Criminal Code Art. 354a bans possession, cultivation and sale; no personal-use threshold. No medical cannabis program. Only low-THC hemp/CBD trade allowed.
BG.punishment: Possession: 1-6 yrs prison plus fine (about EUR 1,000-5,000); minor cases fine up to about EUR 500 (still criminal). Trafficking: 2-8 yrs plus fine, more if aggravated.
BG.access: No legal access. No medical program.

BH.name: Bahrain
BH.headline: Strictly illegal; hashish trafficking has drawn death sentences
BH.law: All use, possession and trade banned under Law No. 15 of 2007 on narcotics.
BH.punishment: Personal use: prison (at least 1 year reported) plus fine; foreigners deported. Trafficking: life prison; law allows death. 4+ on drug death row (HRI).
BH.tourists: No. Illegal for everyone; foreigners also face deportation.
BH.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: Feb 2019: High Criminal Court sentenced 2 men to death over 68 kg hashish shipped from Iran (upheld on appeal May 2019); 2022 hashish death sentence later reduced to life. Death or life for trafficking-intent import/production/possession of narcotics incl. cannabis (Law 15/2007 art.30(a)); death mandatory if aggravated, e.g. repeat offence or intl syndicate (art.30(b)). Hashish death sentences imposed 2019 and 2022; 4+ on drug death row (HRI).

BI.name: Burundi
BI.headline: Illegal; criminal penalties
BI.law: Cannabis (urumogi) is a prohibited narcotic under Burundi's Penal Code (revised 2017). Use, possession, cultivation and sale are crimes. Burundi abolished the death penalty in 2009.
BI.punishment: Possession and trafficking both carry prison terms and fines; exact ranges not verified. No death penalty (abolished 2009).
BI.access: No legal access. No medical program.
BI.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.

BJ.name: Benin
BJ.headline: Illegal; possession can bring years in prison
BJ.law: Law 97-025 (1997) bans cannabis cultivation and trafficking nationwide; the 2018 Penal Code (Law 2018-16) also criminalizes possession. No medical or hemp program.
BJ.punishment: Possession: reportedly 2-5 years plus 500,000-5M CFA fine (unverified against official text). Trafficking: longer prison terms and heavy fines.
BJ.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
BJ.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

BN.name: Brunei
BN.headline: Illegal; trafficking over 500 g carries the death penalty
BN.law: Misuse of Drugs Act (Cap. 27), modelled on Singapore's, bans use, possession and sale. Large amounts are presumed trafficking. Sharia Penal Code also applies to Muslims.
BN.punishment: Possession/use: prison and fines, plus caning for some offences. Trafficking: long prison terms + caning; >500 g cannabis: death penalty. No executions since 1957.
BN.access: No legal access. No medical program.
BN.tourists: No. Visitors face the same law; drug tests possible.
BN.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: Feb 2017: Malaysian Muhammad Mustaqim Mustofa bin Abdullah sentenced to hang for possessing over 6 kg cannabis for trafficking; also Lam Ming Hwa sentenced to death 2004 for 922 g cannabis. Trafficking >500 g cannabis: death. Not carried out since 1957 (HRI: symbolic).

BO.name: Bolivia
BO.headline: Illegal; users can be committed to treatment, traffickers get long terms
BO.law: Law 1008 (1988, partly replaced by Law 913 of 2017) bans cannabis. Art. 49 treats users caught with a 48-hour supply as subject to compulsory treatment; anything more is presumed trafficking. No threshold table and no medical program.
BO.punishment: Personal use: compulsory internment in a rehab facility; above a 48-hour supply, prosecuted as possession/trafficking. Trafficking (Art. 48): 10-25 years prison.
BO.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis program.

BR.name: Brazil
BR.headline: Up to 40 g or 6 female plants is an administrative matter, not a crime
BR.law: Anvisa approved cultivation rules on 28 Jan 2026 (RDC 1.013/2026, published 3 Feb 2026, in force 4 Aug 2026). They allow only licensed legal entities to grow low-THC (0.3% or less) cannabis for medical, pharmaceutical and research use. Patient associations get rules (RDC 1.014/2026) but still may not sell.
BR.punishment: Personal use: administrative measures only (warning, educational course), no criminal record. Trafficking (Art. 33, Law 11.343): 5-15 years prison plus fine.
BR.access: No recreational shops. Medical: prescription CBD/THC products in pharmacies (Anvisa RDC 327/2019) or imported; patient associations; home grow for patients via court habeas corpus.
BR.tourists: Same personal-use rules; no legal place to buy.
BR.home_grow: Up to 6 female plants presumed personal use (administrative)
BR.medical: Legal: pharmacy products, imports, court-authorized patient grow

BS.name: Bahamas
BS.headline: Medical/religious cannabis law passed 2024 but licensing not yet launched
BS.law: Cannabis Act 2024 (passed July 2024) creates medical, scientific and Rastafari religious use and a fixed $250 ticket for up to 30 g. Only the Cannabis Authority sections are in force; until commencement, the Dangerous Drugs Act still governs.
BS.punishment: Under Dangerous Drugs Act (still operative): possession can bring fines up to $120,000 and up to 10 yrs; supply/trafficking heavier. Once in force: up to 30 g = $250 ticket, no conviction.
BS.access: None yet: Cannabis Authority delayed launch of licensing (July 2026). Future prescriptions via trained doctors and licensed dispensaries.
BS.medical: Cannabis Act 2024 passed; Authority set up, no licences or dispensing yet (2026)

BT.name: Bhutan
BT.headline: Illegal; cannabis grows wild but possession and sale are crimes
BT.law: Narcotic Drugs, Psychotropic Substances and Substance Abuse Act 2015 (amended 2018) bans possession, sale, cultivation and use of cannabis, which grows wild across the country.
BT.punishment: Small-quantity possession/use: graded as a misdemeanour (short prison term or fine; treatment options). Trafficking/sale: felony with multi-year prison terms.

BW.name: Botswana
BW.headline: Illegal for adults; Cannabis Act 2025 licenses medical and industrial use
BW.law: Parliament passed the Cannabis Act in Aug 2025; regulations followed in Jan 2026 and a National Cannabis Control Authority now licenses cultivation and processing. Recreational use stays illegal under the 2018 narcotics act.
BW.punishment: Recreational possession and trafficking are crimes under the Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 2018 (fines and prison); exact ranges not verified.
BW.access: No personal access. A licensed medical, research and industrial sector is starting, with pilot cultivation licences reported in 2026.
BW.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.

BY.name: Belarus
BY.headline: Harsh prohibition; any possession is a crime; no death penalty for drugs
BY.law: Criminal Code Art. 328 criminalises possession of any amount, cultivation and sale. No medical program. Belarus keeps the death penalty, but drug offences are not among capital crimes.
BY.punishment: Possession without intent to sell: up to 5 yrs restriction of liberty or 2-5 yrs prison. Selling: 3-8 yrs; aggravated or organised: up to 15-20 yrs.
BY.access: No legal access. No medical program.
BY.death_detail: Belarus retains capital punishment, but drug offences (Art. 328) carry prison terms only.

BZ.name: Belize
BZ.headline: Up to 10 g on private premises not an offence; legalisation bill stalled
BZ.law: Misuse of Drugs (Amendment) Act 2017: adults may possess up to 10 g on private premises without criminal penalty. Sale, cultivation and import stay illegal. 2022 Cannabis Licensing Bill (adult-use market) is parked pending a deferred referendum.
BZ.punishment: Up to 10 g in private: no offence; in public/schools: fine. Over 10 g: criminal; 60 g+ presumed trafficking — heavy fines and multi-year prison.
BZ.access: No legal access: no shops, no medical program, no lawful home grow.
BZ.tourists: Small private possession tolerated; no legal place to buy.

CA.name: Canada
CA.headline: Fully legal nationwide since 2018 with licensed stores
CA.law: Cannabis Act (17 Oct 2018) legalised adult possession, purchase from licensed retailers, and home growing. Provinces set age, retail model and public-use rules. Sale outside the licensed system is a crime.
CA.punishment: Over 30 g in public: ticket or up to 5 yrs less a day. Illegal sale/distribution or production: up to 14 yrs. Selling to minors: up to 14 yrs.
CA.access: Very easy: licensed provincial/private stores and government online shops; home grow of 4 plants (not in Quebec/Manitoba); separate federal medical access via licensed producers.
CA.tourists: Yes — adult visitors can buy at licensed stores; never carry across the border.
CA.age: 18+ to 21+ by province (19 most; 18 AB; 21 QC)
CA.home_grow: 4 plants per household (banned in QC, MB)
CA.medical: Federal medical program since 2001 (now under Cannabis Regulations)
CA.subnational: Age 18 (AB), 19 (most), 21 (QC); Quebec and Manitoba ban home grow; retail is public in some provinces, private in others.

CD.name: DR Congo
CD.headline: Illegal; widely grown but use and sale are crimes
CD.law: Cannabis is prohibited under DRC drug legislation. Cultivation, possession, use and sale are crimes, though it is widely grown and used. No medical or hemp program.
CD.punishment: Use/possession: prison and fines. Trafficking: long prison terms. Exact current ranges not verified.
CD.access: No legal access for individuals. A 2021 health-ministry order provides licensed industrial growing of low-THC (0.2% or less) medical cannabis by companies.
CD.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.
CD.medical: Licensing framework on paper: Ministerial Order 1250 of 2 March 2021 lets licensed Congolese companies grow 'cannabis for medical use' industrially (only varieties with 0.2% THC or less and high CBD); no patient program
CD.subnational: Conflict-affected eastern provinces have weak enforcement; national law still applies.

CF.name: Central African Republic
CF.headline: Illegal; use and trafficking are criminal
CF.law: Cannabis is prohibited under the Penal Code and drug-control law. Cultivation, possession, use and sale are crimes. No medical program. Death penalty abolished 2024.
CF.punishment: Use/possession: prison and fines. Trafficking: long prison terms. Exact current ranges not verified.
CF.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
CF.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.
CF.subnational: Large areas are outside effective state control; national law still applies.

CG.name: Republic of the Congo
CG.headline: Illegal; use and trafficking are criminal
CG.law: Cannabis is prohibited under national drug-control and penal laws. Cultivation, possession, use and sale are crimes. No medical program.
CG.punishment: Use/possession: prison and fines. Trafficking: long prison terms. Exact current ranges not verified.
CG.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
CG.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.headline: CHF 100 fine for use; city pilot sales; legalisation bill in parliament
CH.law: Cannabis over 1% THC is illegal, but since 2013 adult use is a CHF 100 fixed fine; the Federal Court (2017) ruled possessing up to 10 g for own use is not punishable. Legal-sale pilot trials run since 2023. A legalisation bill (CanPG) is in parliamentary committee.
CH.punishment: Use: CHF 100 fixed fine; up to 10 g for personal use not punishable. Dealing/cultivation: up to 3 years or fine; aggravated cases at least 1 year (up to 20).
CH.access: Pilot trials (Basel, Zurich, Bern, Lausanne, Geneva, others) sell legally to enrolled adult residents of those cities. Legal CBD shops (under 1% THC). Medical: doctors may prescribe since Aug 2022.
CH.tourists: No legal THC purchase; pilots are residents-only. CBD (under 1% THC) is legal to buy.
CH.medical: Since Aug 2022 doctors prescribe without federal permit
CH.subnational: Pilot trials only in participating cities; enforcement varies by canton.

CI.name: Côte d'Ivoire
CI.headline: Illegal; users get short jail or treatment orders, dealers long terms
CI.law: Law 2022-407 (June 2022) replaced the 1988 drug law: cannabis use, possession, cultivation and sale stay crimes, but users are treated as patients, with court-ordered treatment as an alternative to prison.
CI.punishment: Use: 1-3 months prison (Art. 10); prosecution dropped if user completes ordered treatment (Art. 19-20). Sale/trafficking: multi-year prison and fines (a 2026 dealer got 24 months + 300,000 CFA).
CI.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
CI.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

CL.name: Chile
CL.headline: Private possession allowed; possession or use in public is fined
CL.law: Law 20.000 (2005) does not punish private consumption or small personal-use possession in private. Public consumption is a misdemeanour. Sale is a crime; growing is a crime unless proven for personal use. Medical prescriptions allowed since 2015 (Decree 84).
CL.punishment: Public use or carrying: fine, community service or treatment. Micro-trafficking (Art. 4): 541 days-5 years. Trafficking (Art. 3): 5 years and 1 day to 15 years prison.
CL.access: No shops. Medical: pharmacy products on a retained prescription. Courts sometimes accept small home grows proven for personal or medical use, but there is no legal right.
CL.tourists: Private use same as locals; no legal place to buy.
CL.home_grow: Illegal (courts may excuse proven personal-use grows)
CL.medical: Legal since 2015; prescription products in pharmacies

CM.name: Cameroon
CM.headline: Illegal; even small possession is a crime
CM.law: Law 97/019 (1997) on narcotics lists cannabis as a Table I drug and criminalizes cultivation, possession, use, transport and sale. No medical or hemp program.
CM.punishment: Use/possession: prison and fines (sources cite fines 25,000-1,250,000 CFA and multi-year terms). Trafficking: 10-20 years. Ranges come from secondary sources.
CM.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
CM.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

CN.name: China
CN.headline: Strictly illegal; large-scale trafficking can be punished by death
CN.law: Cannabis is a controlled narcotic under the Criminal Law and Anti-Drug Law. Use and possession are banned; any sale or trafficking is a crime regardless of quantity (Art. 347). No reform; CBD banned in cosmetics since 2021.
CN.punishment: Use/small possession: 10–15 days administrative detention + fine; addicts face compulsory rehab. Trafficking: prison; 'large quantities' (e.g. ≥150 kg leaf, ≥10 kg resin, ≥5 kg oil) = 15 yrs, life or death. Executions are state secrets.
CN.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis program; industrial hemp (low-THC) is grown under licence in Yunnan and Heilongjiang only.
CN.tourists: No. Foreigners are detained/deported; Chinese police punish citizens who used cannabis abroad.
CN.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: 16 Sept 1998: three men sentenced to death in Guangdong for smuggling over 4 tonnes of marijuana from Cambodia (Amnesty). No recent cannabis-specific case found; law still capital for trafficking. Art. 347: trafficking large quantities (≥150 kg leaf/≥10 kg resin/≥5 kg oil per 2016 SPC rules) → death possible. China: HRI 'high application'.
CN.subnational: Hong Kong: possession up to 7 yrs, trafficking up to life; CBD banned 2023. Macau: use 3 mo–1 yr, trafficking 5–15 yrs. No death penalty in either.

CO.name: Colombia
CO.headline: Up to 20 g for personal use is protected; sales illegal; strong medical sector
CO.law: Constitutional Court ruling C-221 (1994) protects carrying and using a personal dose: up to 20 g (Law 30 of 1986). Sale remains illegal. Adult-use market bills (Bill 023 of 2025) were still in Congress as of Sept 2026, not law.
CO.punishment: Personal dose: no crime (public-space use can draw police-code measures). Trafficking (Penal Code Art. 376): 64-108 months prison for up to 1 kg; 128-360 months for larger amounts.
CO.access: No legal shops. Up to 20 plants for personal use tolerated. Medical: licensed producers; prescription products in pharmacies (Law 1787 of 2016, Decree 811 of 2021).
CO.tourists: Can possess a personal dose like locals; no legal place to buy.
CO.home_grow: Up to 20 plants for personal use
CO.medical: Legal since 2016; prescriptions filled at pharmacies

CR.name: Costa Rica
CR.headline: Personal use not a crime; medical law in force since 2022, rollout slow
CR.law: Law 8204 punishes possession only for trafficking or sale; personal consumption is treated as a public-health matter, not a crime. Sale and growing remain illegal. Law 10113 (2022) legalized medical cannabis and hemp; regulations approved Feb 2025.
CR.punishment: Personal use: no criminal penalty; police may confiscate. Trafficking, sale or cultivation (Art. 58, Law 8204): 8-15 years prison.
CR.access: No recreational supply. Medical: THC products only via pharmacies with a prescription under Law 10113; licensing of producers is still slow, so supply is limited.
CR.tourists: No legal purchase; personal use is tolerated but sourcing is illegal.
CR.medical: Legal since 2022 (Law 10113); pharmacy prescription products, limited supply

CU.name: Cuba
CU.headline: Illegal; the law allows death for trafficking, but no death sentence for marijuana is documented
CU.law: All cannabis use, possession, growing and sale is illegal under the 2022 Penal Code (Law 151, Arts. 235–236). No medical or religious exemption. Courts treat 1 lb (460 g) as a 'relatively large' quantity.
CU.punishment: Possession (Art. 236) is a crime with prison terms. Trafficking (Art. 235): 4–10 yrs basic; 10–30 yrs, life or death for international trafficking or large quantities. Recent marijuana dealing cases drew 8–9 yrs.
CU.access: No legal access. No medical program.
CU.tourists: No — tourists are prosecuted; marijuana bales washing ashore have led to arrests.
CU.death_detail: Art. 235(2)(g): 10–30 yrs, life or death when drug offences involve 'relatively large quantities' (judicial norm 1 lb / 460 g, any drug incl. marijuana). HRI 2025: symbolic; no executions in 20+ yrs.

CV.name: Cabo Verde
CV.headline: Illegal; trafficking punished with long prison terms
CV.law: Law 78/IV/93 (1993) on drugs bans cultivation, possession, use and trafficking of cannabis. No medical or hemp program. Islands are a transatlantic cocaine transit point.
CV.punishment: Use/possession: offence with lighter penalties (fines/short prison). Trafficking: multi-year prison terms. Exact current ranges not verified.
CV.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
CV.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

CY.name: Cyprus
CY.headline: State medical program; recreational possession is a crime, usually fined
CY.law: Cannabis is a controlled drug; possession, cultivation and sale are crimes. Medical cannabis oil legal since 2017, widened to more conditions in 2019 under a state-regulated program.
CY.punishment: Personal possession: first offenders typically fined about EUR 400-1,000 or sent to rehab; prison possible. Over 30 g or 3 plants treated as trafficking: long prison terms, up to life.
CY.access: Medical only: specialist prescription for qualifying conditions under the state program. No shops, clubs or home grow.
CY.medical: Yes since 2017 (expanded 2019): state program, qualifying patients
CY.subnational: Figures cover the Republic of Cyprus; the Turkish-controlled north applies its own, strict law.

CZ.name: Czechia
CZ.headline: Home grow and possession legal for adults 21+ since 1 Jan 2026; no sales
CZ.law: Criminal Code amendment in force 1 Jan 2026: adults 21+ may grow 3 plants at home and hold 100 g dried at home, 25 g in public. Commercial sale remains illegal; no shops or clubs. Medical cannabis legal since 2013.
CZ.punishment: Over limits: 4-5 plants or 101-200 g home (26-50 g public) is a fine-only offence; above that is criminal. Selling or dealing remains a crime: up to 5 yrs, longer for large scale.
CZ.access: Grow your own (3 plants) or medical prescription via pharmacies (insurance covers most of cost). No legal retail, no clubs, no gifting market.
CZ.tourists: Adults 21+ can possess up to 25 g in public, but there is no legal place to buy.
CZ.medical: Yes since 2013: prescription via pharmacies, largely insurance-covered

DE.name: Germany
DE.headline: Legal since 2024: possess 25 g, grow 3 plants, join a non-profit club
DE.law: The Cannabis Act (KCanG), effective 1 Apr 2024, lets adults possess 25 g in public and 50 g at home, grow 3 plants, and join non-profit clubs (since 1 Jul 2024). Commercial sale is illegal. The 2025 coalition kept the law pending evaluation (interim report Apr 2026).
DE.punishment: Over 25 g (to 30 g) in public: fine. Over 30 g public / 60 g home: up to 3 years or fine. Unlicensed sale: up to 3 years; serious cases 3 months-5 years; selling to minors or armed: 2+ years.
DE.access: No shops. Clubs: max 500 members, 18+, 6 months' German residence, 3-month minimum membership; 25 g/day, 50 g/month (18-20: 30 g, max 10% THC). Medical: prescription via pharmacies; telemedicine common.
DE.tourists: May possess and use up to 25 g, but no legal source: clubs are residents-only.
DE.medical: Prescription via pharmacies (MedCanG 2024); bill to curb telemedicine/flower mail-order pending
DE.subnational: No use near schools/playgrounds or in pedestrian zones before 8pm; Bavaria enforces strictly.

DJ.name: Djibouti
DJ.headline: Illegal; khat is legal, cannabis is not
DJ.law: Cannabis is a prohibited narcotic under Djibouti's penal code. Possession, use and sale are crimes. Khat is legal and widely used, but cannabis is not. Djibouti has abolished the death penalty.
DJ.punishment: Possession and trafficking both carry prison terms and fines; exact ranges not verified. No death penalty (abolished).
DJ.access: No legal access. No medical program.
DJ.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.

DK.name: Denmark
DK.headline: Illegal; small possession fined; medical cannabis pilot since 2018
DK.law: Possession, cultivation and sale are illegal under the Euphoriant Substances Act and Penal Code. Christiania's Pusher Street open market was shut down in 2024. A medical cannabis pilot lets doctors prescribe since 1 Jan 2018.
DK.punishment: Small personal possession: fine (first offence typically a few thousand DKK); legal max 2 years. Trafficking: up to 10 years; aggravated cases up to 16 years.
DK.access: No recreational access. Medical: any doctor may prescribe approved cannabis products under the pilot (partly subsidised), dispensed at pharmacies.
DK.tourists: No legal purchase; Christiania sales are illegal and now largely gone.
DK.medical: Pilot since 2018 (doctor prescription, pharmacies); extended, permanence under review

DM.name: Dominica
DM.headline: Up to 28 g and 3 plants not prosecuted since 2020
DM.law: Drugs (Prevention of Misuse) (Amendment) Act 2020: adults 18+ may possess up to 28 g (1 oz) and grow 3 plants at home without prosecution. Sale and public use remain illegal. No medical law passed.
DM.punishment: Up to 28 g: no prosecution. Above the limit, cultivation for sale or trafficking: criminal charges with fines and prison.
DM.access: Home grow only (3 plants). No shops, dispensaries or medical program.
DM.tourists: Small amounts tolerated; no legal place to buy.
DM.medical: None; medical law promised but not passed

DO.name: Dominican Republic
DO.headline: Strictly illegal; even small amounts can mean prison
DO.law: Law 50-88 on Drugs bans possession, use, cultivation and distribution in any amount, grading offenders by quantity: under 20 g = simple possessor, 20 g–1 lb = distributor, over 1 lb = trafficker. Foreign medical cards are not valid.
DO.punishment: Under 20 g: about 6 months–2 yrs + fine (treatment possible). Distributor (20 g–1 lb): about 3–10 yrs. Trafficking or cultivation: 5–20 yrs and RD$50,000–250,000 fines.
DO.access: No legal access. No medical program; US medical cards not recognised.
DO.tourists: No — tourists are arrested and jailed.

DZ.name: Algeria
DZ.headline: Illegal; the law allows death for trafficking, but no death sentence for marijuana is documented
DZ.law: All use, possession and trade banned under Law 04-18 (2004), toughened by Law 25-03 (July 2025), which adds treatment options for users and death for serious trafficking.
DZ.punishment: Personal use: prison (about 2 months-2 years) or court-ordered treatment. Trafficking: up to life; death if aggravated (organised crime, firearms, deaths caused, near schools). Moratorium on executions since 1993.
DZ.tourists: No. Visitors face the same penalties.
DZ.death_detail: Law 25-03 (2025) allows death for aggravated drug trafficking, cannabis included. First sentences were for cocaine/ecstasy; no executions since 1993.

EC.name: Ecuador
EC.headline: Use not a crime, but the 10 g table was scrapped in 2023; case by case now
EC.law: Constitution (Art. 364) bars criminalizing consumption. Noboa repealed the 2013 table (10 g) in Nov 2023. The 2025 Ley de Solidaridad says new 'parameters' will be set by Health, Prosecutor and Judiciary; until then prosecutors judge each case.
EC.punishment: Personal use: not punishable if accepted as personal. Trafficking (COIP Art. 220): prison scaled by quantity, from about 1-3 years for minimal amounts up to 10-13 years for large scale.
EC.access: No recreational sales. Medical: cannabis medicines legal since 2019 COIP reform; prescription products via pharmacies; hemp (under 1% THC) regulated.
EC.tourists: No legal purchase; small personal amounts not a crime but no safe threshold exists.
EC.possession_limit: no fixed threshold (10 g table repealed Nov 2023)

EE.name: Estonia
EE.headline: Up to 7.5 g is a misdemeanour (fine); larger amounts and sale are crimes
EE.law: Narcotic Drugs Act: possessing a small amount (up to about 7.5 g herbal cannabis) is a misdemeanour since 2002, not a crime. Larger amounts, cultivation and sale are criminal. Cannabinoid medicines only case by case.
EE.punishment: Small amount: fine up to EUR 1,200 or up to 30 days detention (rare). Large amount: criminal, up to 5 yrs. Trafficking: 1-10 yrs; up to 15 yrs if aggravated.
EE.access: No legal purchase. Cannabinoid medicines only by special case-by-case prescription; no plant program, no shops or home grow.
EE.tourists: No legal purchase; possession risks a fine.
EE.medical: Very limited: cannabinoid medicines case by case; no national program

EG.name: Egypt
EG.headline: Illegal; hashish common, but trafficking can carry death
EG.law: All use, possession and trade banned under Law No. 182 of 1960 on narcotics (amended); cannabis is a Schedule 1 drug.
EG.punishment: Personal use/possession: prison plus EGP 10,000-50,000 fine; courts may order treatment. Import/export/cultivation for trade: death. 7+ drug death sentences in 2025 (HRI).
EG.tourists: No. Visitors face the same penalties.
EG.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: Jun 2013: Red Sea Criminal Court (Hurghada) sentenced a Briton, 3 Seychellois and a Pakistani (in absentia) to death for smuggling 3 t of cannabis; Grand Mufti approved. Death for import, export or production for trafficking (Law 182/1960). 7+ drug death sentences in 2025 (HRI).

ER.name: Eritrea
ER.headline: Illegal; criminal penalties, little public information
ER.law: Cannabis is a prohibited narcotic. Possession, use, cultivation and sale are criminal offences under Eritrea's 2015 Penal Code and drug rules. No reform has been reported.
ER.punishment: Possession and trafficking both carry prison terms; exact ranges not verified. Detention practices are opaque. Not on HRI's list of drug death-penalty states.
ER.access: No legal access. No medical program.
ER.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.

ES.name: Spain
ES.headline: Private possession allowed; possession or use in public is fined
ES.law: Private use and growing for personal use are not crimes. Public possession or use is an administrative offence under the 2015 Citizen Security Law. Sale is a crime. Royal Decree 903/2025 (Oct 2025) created a hospital-only medical cannabis framework.
ES.punishment: Public possession/use: fine €601-30,000 (usually €601+). Visible plants: fine. Trafficking: 1-3 years plus fine for cannabis; aggravated cases (large amounts, near schools) up to about 4.5 years or more.
ES.access: Private cannabis social clubs operate in a legal grey zone (esp. Catalonia, Basque Country); membership by referral, often residence/waiting rules. Medical: specialist prescription, hospital pharmacies only.
ES.tourists: No legal purchase; club access for visitors is legally dubious.
ES.possession_limit: personal amount in private (no fixed g)
ES.home_grow: Tolerated in private if not visible from public; no set plant limit
ES.subnational: Regional club laws were struck down; clubs most common in Catalonia and Basque Country.

ET.name: Ethiopia
ET.headline: Illegal; selling cannabis brings 5-10 years in prison
ET.law: Criminal Code 2004 (art. 525) bans cultivating, making, possessing, using or trafficking narcotic plants, cannabis included. Despite the Rastafarian community at Shashamane, there is no exemption.
ET.punishment: Sale or trafficking: 5-10 years' rigorous imprisonment plus a fine of up to 100,000 birr (reported). Personal use or possession: imprisonment, reportedly up to about 5 years.
ET.access: No legal access. No medical program.
ET.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.

FI.name: Finland
FI.headline: Illegal; use is fined; medical cannabis only by special permit
FI.law: Use, possession, cultivation and sale are crimes under the Criminal Code (ch. 50). A 2024 citizens' initiative to legalise did not pass. Medical cannabis is an unlicensed medicine needing a special permit from Fimea.
FI.punishment: Drug use offence (small personal amount): fine or up to 6 months; first-timers may be waived. Drug offence: up to 2 years; aggravated: 1-10 years.
FI.access: No recreational access. Medical: Sativex on prescription; flower or oil only with a Fimea special permit after other treatments fail; very rare.
FI.medical: Very limited: Sativex; Fimea special permits for flower/oil

FJ.name: Fiji
FJ.headline: Illegal; tough law, medicinal cannabis law only being studied
FJ.law: Cannabis is an illicit drug under the Illicit Drugs Control Act 2004; possession, cultivation and supply are crimes. Cabinet approved a medicinal cannabis feasibility study and drafting in late 2024; a Counter Narcotics Bill was in consultation in 2026. Nothing enacted.
FJ.punishment: Statutory max for possession or supply: life and/or F$1m fine. In practice small amounts (under 100 g) often get non-custodial sentences; larger quantities and trafficking bring long prison terms.
FJ.access: No legal access. No medical program yet (legislation under study since 2024).
FJ.medical: None in force; medicinal cannabis study/drafting approved late 2024
FJ.death_detail: No death penalty; abolished. 2026 calls to reinstate it for drug crimes, not law.

FM.name: Micronesia
FM.headline: Illegal nationally; no medical program
FM.law: Cannabis is a controlled substance under FSM national law and state laws (Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae); possession, cultivation and sale are criminal. No legalisation or medical law found.
FM.punishment: Possession and trafficking are criminal offences with prison and fines; maximums vary by national and state law and were not confirmed.
FM.access: No legal access. No medical program.

FR.name: France
FR.headline: Strictly illegal; €200 on-the-spot fines; medical pilot still running
FR.law: Use, possession, cultivation and sale are crimes under the Public Health Code. Since 2020 police can issue a fixed criminal fine (amende forfaitaire délictuelle) for use. A medical pilot began 2021; the permanent framework is still not in force as of 2026.
FR.punishment: Use/possession: up to 1 year and €3,750, usually a €200 fixed fine (€150 if paid fast, €450 if late). Trafficking: up to 10 years and €7.5M; organised production/import up to 20-30 years.
FR.access: No recreational access. Medical: only patients already enrolled in the ANSM pilot (since 2021, extended repeatedly) receive cannabis medicines via hospital and pharmacy. CBD products under 0.3% THC are sold legally.
FR.medical: ANSM pilot since 2021, extended; permanent decree pending, wider access expected 2027

GA.name: Gabon
GA.headline: Illegal; use and trafficking are criminal
GA.law: Cannabis is prohibited under Gabon's Penal Code (2019) and drug laws. Cultivation, possession, use and sale are crimes. No medical program.
GA.punishment: Use/possession: prison and fines. Trafficking: long prison terms. Exact current ranges not verified.
GA.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
GA.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.headline: Illegal Class B drug; specialist medical prescriptions allowed since 2018
GB.law: Cannabis is a Class B drug under the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971. Possession, cultivation and supply are criminal offences. Since 1 Nov 2018, specialist doctors may prescribe cannabis-based medicinal products.
GB.punishment: Possession: up to 5 years and/or unlimited fine (police often issue a cannabis warning or £90 penalty notice for small amounts). Supply/production: up to 14 years and/or unlimited fine.
GB.access: No recreational access. Medical: specialist-only prescriptions, mostly through private clinics; NHS prescriptions are rare (mainly severe epilepsy, MS spasticity, chemo nausea). Dispensed by pharmacies.
GB.tourists: No legal purchase or use; UK prescriptions only.
GB.medical: Since Nov 2018: specialist prescription; mostly private clinics, NHS access very limited
GB.subnational: Scotland uses recorded police warnings for small amounts; penalties set UK-wide.

GD.name: Grenada
GD.headline: 2026 law: adults 21+ may hold 56 g and grow 4 registered plants
GD.law: Drug Abuse (Prevention and Control) (Amendment) Act 2026 (passed Jan 2026, gazetted Feb 2026 per secondary source): adults 21+ may possess 56 g (15 g resin) and grow 4 plants per registered household. Public use and sale remain prohibited; Rastafari sacrament protected.
GD.punishment: Within limits: no penalty. Ages 18–20: rehab/counselling, no record. Public use: fixed penalty. 71 g+ (30 g resin) is a 'trafficable quantity': trafficking charges, prison.
GD.access: Home grow after registration (system still being set up). No licensed shops or medical program yet.
GD.tourists: Possession within limits allowed for 21+; no legal place to buy.

GE.name: Georgia
GE.headline: Using is not punished, but possession was tightened in 2025
GE.law: Constitutional Court rulings (2017-2018) made cannabis consumption non-punishable (except public places/near children). July 2025 amendments put cannabis back with other drugs: possession over 5 g dried is a crime again. Sale remains criminal.
GE.punishment: Up to 5 g dried (10 g fresh): administrative fine; repeat can mean up to 1 yr. 5-70 g dried: up to 6 yrs. 70-250 g: 5-8 yrs. Sale/production: multi-year to life for very large amounts.
GE.access: No legal source: consumption is tolerated, but buying and selling stay illegal, so users must buy on the black market.
GE.tourists: Use itself is not punished, but buying is illegal; same rules for visitors.

GH.name: Ghana
GH.headline: Recreational illegal; licensed low-THC hemp for industry/medicine only
GH.law: Narcotics Control Commission Act 2020 (Act 1019) made personal-use possession fine-only. Act 1100 (2023) + L.I. 2475 allow licensed growing of cannabis with THC at or under 0.3% for industrial/medicinal use. First licences: Aug 2026.
GH.punishment: Personal-use possession: fine (200-500 penalty units), no jail under Act 1019. Unlicensed cultivation, supply and trafficking: long prison terms (statute minimums of 10+ years).
GH.access: Licensed cultivation only for companies, via NACOC/Interior Ministry; THC capped at 0.3%. First 2 licences issued Aug 2026. No retail sales or patient prescription system.
GH.tourists: No. Recreational purchase or use is illegal.
GH.medical: Industrial/medicinal hemp licensing (THC 0.3% max); no patient dispensing program

GM.name: Gambia
GM.headline: Illegal; first-time small possession gets fines, trafficking up to life
GM.law: Drug Control Act 2003, amended 2014 (created DLEAG). Possession, use, cultivation and sale of cannabis are crimes. Death penalty for drugs was repealed in 2011 and replaced by life imprisonment.
GM.punishment: First offence 0.1-150 g: fine D50,000-100,000 or 6-12 months prison, or both. Trafficking: long prison terms up to life imprisonment.
GM.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
GM.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

GN.name: Guinea
GN.headline: Illegal; use and trafficking are criminal offences
GN.law: Cannabis is banned under Guinea's drug provisions in the Penal Code (2016) and drug-control law. Cultivation, possession, use and sale are crimes. No medical or hemp program.
GN.punishment: Use/possession: prison and fines. Trafficking: multi-year prison terms with heavy fines. Exact current ranges not verified.
GN.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
GN.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

GQ.name: Equatorial Guinea
GQ.headline: Illegal; use and trafficking are criminal
GQ.law: Cannabis is prohibited under national drug and penal laws. Cultivation, possession, use and sale are crimes. No medical program. Death penalty abolished 2022.
GQ.punishment: Use/possession: prison and fines. Trafficking: long prison terms. Exact current ranges not verified.
GQ.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
GQ.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

GR.name: Greece
GR.headline: Medical legal since 2017 (pharmacies since 2024); personal use still criminal
GR.law: Law 4139/2013: possession for personal use is a criminal offence, but low-level. Medical cannabis legal since 2017; pharmacy dispensing began Feb 2024. Sale and cultivation are crimes.
GR.punishment: Personal use: up to 5 months prison, often suspended; no record if no repeat in 5 yrs. Trafficking: 8+ yrs and heavy fines; life for aggravated cases.
GR.access: Medical only: doctor's prescription filled at pharmacies (since 2024). No shops, clubs or legal home grow.
GR.medical: Yes since 2017; pharmacy prescriptions since Feb 2024

GT.name: Guatemala
GT.headline: Illegal; even possession for personal use can mean prison
GT.law: Ley contra la Narcoactividad (Decree 48-92) bans use, possession, cultivation and sale. Art. 39 makes possession for personal consumption a crime; there is no gram threshold, so judges decide case by case what counts as personal use.
GT.punishment: Possession for own use: 4 months to 2 years prison plus Q200-Q10,000 fine (Art. 39). Trafficking/storage: 12-20 years prison plus heavy fines.
GT.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis program.
GT.tourists: No. Same criminal penalties apply to visitors.

GW.name: Guinea-Bissau
GW.headline: Illegal; drug laws criminalize use and trafficking
GW.law: Drug law (Decree-Law 2-B/93, 1993) prohibits cultivation, possession, use and trafficking of cannabis. No medical or hemp exception. Country is a major cocaine transit hub; enforcement is uneven.
GW.punishment: Use/possession: criminal, prison and/or fines possible. Trafficking: multi-year prison terms. Exact current ranges not verified.
GW.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
GW.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

GY.name: Guyana
GY.headline: No jail for up to 30 g since 2022; counselling or community service instead
GY.law: Narcotic Drugs (Amendment) Act 2022 removed prison for up to 30 g: up to 15 g brings counselling, 15-30 g community service. It remains an offence. Over 30 g is presumed trafficking. Sale and growing illegal; no medical program.
GY.punishment: Up to 30 g: counselling or community service, no prison. Above 30 g: trafficking charges with prison terms and heavy fines under the Narcotic Drugs Act.
GY.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis program.
GY.tourists: No legal purchase; small amounts are non-custodial offences.

HN.name: Honduras
HN.headline: Illegal to possess, grow, sell or transport; no medical program
HN.law: Cannabis is illegal under the drug law and the 2020 Penal Code. Personal-use possession is not clearly exempt and no gram threshold is defined; small amounts may draw fines or treatment, larger amounts are treated as trafficking. Medical bills (2022) never passed.
HN.punishment: Personal possession: fines, treatment or possible detention at police/court discretion. Trafficking under the 2020 Penal Code: about 4-7 years for less harmful drugs, up to 10-15 years when aggravated, plus day-fines.
HN.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis program.

HR.name: Croatia
HR.headline: Small possession is a misdemeanour (fine) since 2013; medical since 2015
HR.law: Since Jan 2013 possession of small amounts for personal use is a misdemeanour, not a crime. Cultivation and sale are crimes. THC-based medicines legal on prescription via pharmacies since Oct 2015.
HR.punishment: Personal possession: fine about EUR 650-2,650 (treatment may be ordered). Trafficking: 1-12 yrs; 3-15 yrs if organised or aggravated.
HR.access: Medical only: doctor's prescription for listed conditions (cancer, MS, epilepsy, AIDS), filled at pharmacies, monthly THC cap. No shops or clubs.
HR.tourists: No legal purchase; police fine tourists for possession.
HR.medical: Yes since 2015: THC preparations by prescription at pharmacies

HT.name: Haiti
HT.headline: Illegal; no medical program; harsh penalties on paper, weak enforcement
HT.law: Cannabis use, possession, cultivation and sale are banned under the 7 Aug 2001 decree on drug trafficking and illicit use (with 1961 law). No reform or medical program.
HT.punishment: Possession: prison terms reported from months to several years plus fines (exact ranges poorly documented). Trafficking: long prison terms, reportedly up to life. Pre-trial detention can last months.
HT.access: No legal access. No medical route.

HU.name: Hungary
HU.headline: Among Europe's strictest; 2025 crackdown toughened penalties further
HU.law: Possession, use, sale and cultivation are crimes; drug use banned in the constitution (2025). A June 2025 law tightened penalties: treatment diversion now requires naming the seller, and repeat offenders lose it. No medical program.
HU.punishment: Small amount for own use: up to 2 yrs (diversion possible once). Larger amounts: 1-5 or 5-10 yrs. Dealing: 2-8 yrs, up to 20 yrs or life for large scale; asset seizure.
HU.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis program.

ID.name: Indonesia
ID.headline: Illegal; selling >1 kg or more than 5 plants can mean death
ID.law: Narcotics Law 35/2009 lists cannabis as Category I (no medical use). Possession, use, cultivation and sale are crimes. Court rejected medical cannabis (2022). New Penal Code (Jan 2026) makes death a sentence with 10-yr probation.
ID.punishment: Use: up to 4 yrs (rehab possible). Since 2 Jan 2026 the Penal Adjustment Law (Law 1/2026) removed statutory minimum terms from the Narcotics Law, so only maximums apply: possession/cultivation up to 12 yrs (life or up to 20 yrs above 1 kg or 5 plants); sale up to 20 yrs; sale above 1 kg or 5 plants: death, life or up to 20 yrs. Death sentences now carry a 10-yr probation under the new Penal Code. 143 drug death sentences in 2025; no executions since 2016.
ID.access: No legal access. No medical program.
ID.tourists: No. Bali arrests of foreigners are frequent; long jail terms.
ID.medical: None; Constitutional Court rejected medical use in 2022.
ID.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: 2 Oct 2018: West Jakarta District Court sentenced Rizky Albar and Rocky Siahaan to death for smuggling 1.3 tonnes of cannabis from Aceh to Jakarta. Art. 114: selling >1 kg or >5 plants → death possible. 143 drug death sentences in 2025; last execution 2016.

IE.name: Ireland
IE.headline: Illegal, but first-time possession can be diverted to health route (2026); medical by prescription
IE.law: Cannabis is controlled under the Misuse of Drugs Acts 1977-2016; possession, cultivation and sale are crimes. A Garda Health Referral Scheme (from 1 Sep 2026) lets first-time simple possession go to HSE health referral instead of prosecution. No legal change.
IE.punishment: Possession: first offence fine up to about €1,000; repeat offences higher fines, third offence up to 1 yr (3 yrs on indictment). Dealing: up to life; €13,000+ worth carries a presumptive 10-year minimum.
IE.access: No recreational access. Medical Cannabis Access Programme (MCAP): consultant prescription for MS spasticity, chemo nausea or refractory epilepsy, approved products only. Other uses need a ministerial licence.
IE.medical: MCAP (legislated 2019, operating since 2021) for 3 conditions; ministerial licence route

IL.name: Israel
IL.headline: Use in private fined, not a crime; large licensed medical program
IL.law: Since April 2019, adult use/possession of a small personal amount in private is an administrative offence (fines) for first and second offences; sale and growing stay criminal. Medical cannabis legal since the 1990s.
IL.punishment: Personal use: NIS 1,000 fine (1st), NIS 2,000 (2nd); 3rd = conditional criminal case; minors and public use excluded. Sale/trafficking: up to 20 years' prison.
IL.access: No legal recreational sales. Medical: doctor licence/prescription (reformed 2023), bought at licensed pharmacies; well over 100,000 patients.
IL.tourists: No legal purchase; foreign medical patients cannot use home-country scripts.
IL.medical: Yes: national licensed program (Health Ministry IMCA), pharmacy dispensing

IN.name: India
IN.headline: Ganja and charas illegal, bhang tolerated; death possible for repeat hash trade
IN.law: NDPS Act 1985 bans ganja (buds) and charas (resin) for possession, sale and cultivation. Bhang (leaves/seeds) is excluded from the federal ban and left to states, so some states license it. Death penalty added 1988; made discretionary in 2014.
IN.punishment: Ganja: small qty (<1 kg) up to 1 yr and/or Rs10,000 fine; commercial (20 kg+) 10-20 yrs + Rs1-2 lakh. Charas: small <100 g, commercial 1 kg+. S.31A: death for repeat conviction involving 20 kg+ hashish.
IN.access: Bhang is sold legally at government-licensed shops in some states (e.g. Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh/Varanasi). Ganja/charas: no legal access. Himachal Pradesh licensing hemp/medical cultivation (2026 rules).
IN.tourists: Visitors can buy bhang where state-licensed; ganja/charas illegal for all.
IN.medical: Licensed Ayurvedic cannabis medicines; state research/cultivation pilots (J&K, Himachal).
IN.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: 2008: Ghulam Mohammed Malik sentenced to death by Special NDPS Court, Mumbai, under s.31A (repeat offence) for 187 kg charas. Bombay HC 2011 made s.31A discretionary; death remains available. NDPS s.31A: discretionary death for repeat offence with 20 kg+ hashish (charas); ganja not listed. Never carried out (HRI: symbolic).
IN.subnational: Bhang legal/licensed in some states, banned in others (e.g. Assam). Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand license hemp/medical cultivation.

IQ.name: Iraq
IQ.headline: Illegal; trafficking carries death, sentences being handed down
IQ.law: All use, possession and trade banned under Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Law No. 50 of 2017.
IQ.punishment: Personal use: 1-3 years' prison plus fine; treatment possible. Trafficking/import/production: death or life. 40+ drug death sentences in 2025, about a fifth for cannabis (HRI).
IQ.tourists: No. Visitors face the same penalties.
IQ.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: Nov 2025: Baghdad court sentenced 3 men to death over 18 kg of hashish (Art. 27/1, Law 50/2017); Sept 2026 Basra court sentenced a foreign national to death for 10.5 kg hashish. HRI 2025: a fifth of 40 official drug death sentences were cannabis. Death or life for import, export or production for trafficking (Law 50/2017); about 8 cannabis-related death sentences in 2025 (HRI).
IQ.subnational: Kurdistan Region applies its own courts but cannabis is likewise illegal.

IR.name: Iran
IR.headline: Illegal; big trafficking cases bring death, executions at record highs
IR.law: All use, possession and trade banned under the Anti-Narcotics Law (1988), amended Nov 2017 to raise death thresholds.
IR.punishment: Use: fines, flogging, compulsory treatment. Trafficking: prison and fines; death above 50 kg of cannabis or with aggravating factors (armed, ringleader, use of minors, prior serious sentence).
IR.tourists: No. Visitors face the same penalties.
IR.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: Sept 2016: 52-year-old man hanged in Lakan Prison, Rasht, convicted over about 100 kg of hashish (IHRNGO citing Gilan judiciary). Most recent IHR case reports name meth/heroin; no 2025 hashish-specific case found. Trafficking over 50 kg or aggravated (2017 law). 955+ drug executions in 2025, 46% of all executions (HRI).

IS.name: Iceland
IS.headline: Illegal; small possession usually a fine
IS.law: Possession, use, cultivation and sale are prohibited under the Narcotics Act (no. 65/1974). Decriminalisation bills (2021 onward) have not passed. Only approved cannabinoid medicines such as Sativex are available.
IS.punishment: Small possession: usually a fine (reported about ISK 35,000+ for a first offence); prison possible. Trafficking: prison, up to 12 years for serious cases under the Penal Code.
IS.access: No legal access. Sativex on prescription only; no medical cannabis program.
IS.medical: No program; Sativex by prescription only

IT.name: Italy
IT.headline: Personal possession is an administrative offence; sale is a crime
IT.law: Under DPR 309/1990, possession for personal use is an administrative offence, not a crime; sale and cultivation are crimes. The 2025 Security Decree (DL 48/2025) banned hemp-flower ('cannabis light') sales. Medical cannabis legal since 2007.
IT.punishment: Personal use: administrative sanctions, e.g. suspension of driving licence, passport or gun permit for 1-3 months for cannabis (2 months-1 year applies to 'hard' drugs in Tables I/III).
IT.access: hemp-flower shops hit by the 2025 ban (Art. 18 DL 48/2025); in July 2026 the Court of Cassation (judgment 25539/2026) ruled flowers cannot be seized unless shown to be intoxicating, and some lower courts have refused to apply the ban
IT.tourists: No legal purchase; foreigners face the same administrative sanctions.
IT.home_grow: Illegal; Supreme Court (2019) excused tiny domestic grows for personal use
IT.medical: Since 2007: prescription via pharmacies; reimbursed in some regions
IT.subnational: Medical reimbursement and access vary by region.

JM.name: Jamaica
JM.headline: Up to 2 oz is a ticket, 5 plants allowed; licensed medical 'herb houses'
JM.law: Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act 2015: possessing up to 2 oz is a non-arrestable petty offence (ticket, no criminal record); households may grow 5 plants; Rastafari may use as sacrament. Licensed medical cannabis industry via the Cannabis Licensing Authority. Recreational sale illegal.
JM.punishment: Up to 2 oz: J$500 fine ticket, no record; public smoking also ticketable. Over 2 oz, dealing or export: criminal charges with fines and prison (multi-year terms on indictment).
JM.access: Fairly easy: licensed retail 'herb houses' sell to patients with a local or foreign prescription; visitors can sign a self-declaration of medical need on site. Home grow of 5 plants.
JM.tourists: Yes via licensed herb houses using a self-declared medical-need form; up to 2 oz is a ticket.
JM.medical: Licensed medical industry (CLA) since 2015; foreigners can buy with self-declaration

JO.name: Jordan
JO.headline: Illegal; the law allows death for trafficking, but no death sentence for marijuana is documented
JO.law: Use, possession and trade banned under the Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances Law No. 23 of 2016 (amended 2021 so a first-time user's record can be cleared).
JO.punishment: Personal use: prison (months to about 2 years) plus fine; first-timers may avoid a record. Trafficking: long hard-labour terms; death in aggravated cases (HRI: symbolic, no recent executions).
JO.tourists: No. Visitors face the same penalties.
JO.death_detail: Death for trafficking any narcotic, incl. cannabis, in association with an international drug gang (Law 23/2016 art.20, read with art.19); also death if an assault on narcotics officers causes death (art.12). No recent drug executions (HRI: symbolic).

JP.name: Japan
JP.headline: Illegal; use itself became a crime in Dec 2024; medicine route opened
JP.law: Revised laws in force 12 Dec 2024 moved cannabis under the Narcotics and Psychotropics Control Act, criminalising use (new) and raising penalties. The same reform permits approved cannabis-derived medicines; strict THC limits on CBD goods.
JP.punishment: Use or possession: up to 7 yrs. Sale/transfer/import: up to 10 yrs, more for profit (up to life with fine for for-profit import). Unlicensed cultivation: up to 10 yrs. No death penalty for drugs.
JP.access: No recreational access. Approved cannabis-derived medicines are legally allowed since Dec 2024, but as of late 2026 essentially none are on the market (Epidiolex still pending).
JP.tourists: No. Visitors are arrested and deported; urine tests now prove 'use'.
JP.medical: Law allows approved cannabis-derived medicines (2024); none widely available yet.

KE.name: Kenya
KE.headline: Illegal; up to 10 years even for personal use
KE.law: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Control) Act 1994 bans possessing, using, growing or selling cannabis (bhang). Legalisation bills and petitions have been floated but none has passed.
KE.punishment: Possession for personal use: up to 10 years; other possession: up to 20 years. Trafficking: life imprisonment plus a fine of KSh 1 million or three times the drugs' value, whichever is greater.
KE.access: No legal access. No medical program.
KE.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.

KG.name: Kyrgyzstan
KG.headline: Illegal; tiny amounts fined, more means prison
KG.law: Criminal Code (2021) art. 267 and the Code of Misdemeanors ban cannabis; wild cannabis grows in the Issyk-Kul and Chuy regions. Possession under the 'significant amount' threshold is a misdemeanour.
KG.punishment: Below threshold: fine. Possession above it: up to about 5 yrs prison. Trafficking/sale: longer prison terms rising with quantity.

KH.name: Cambodia
KH.headline: Illegal, though loosely enforced in tourist spots; no death penalty
KH.law: The 2012 Law on Drug Control bans cannabis use, possession, cultivation and sale. Enforcement is uneven and 'happy pizza' sales persist, but these remain illegal. No reform.
KH.punishment: Users: compulsory treatment and/or short prison. Possession and trafficking: prison terms rising with quantity, up to life for large-scale trafficking. Exact ranges unverified.
KH.access: No legal access. No medical program.
KH.tourists: No. Tolerance is informal; foreigners can be jailed or deported.
KH.death_detail: Cambodia's constitution abolished the death penalty (1989/1993).

KI.name: Kiribati
KI.headline: Illegal; prohibited for any use
KI.law: Cannabis is prohibited under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance; possession, cultivation, import and sale are criminal. Even foreign medical cannabis is treated as a prohibited import.
KI.punishment: Cultivation/possession: up to 10 yrs prison and/or A$2,000 fine; small amounts often fined (about $300 in one case). Supply/trafficking: prison likely.
KI.access: No legal access. No medical program; foreign prescriptions not recognised.
KI.tourists: No. Illegal, including medical cannabis brought from abroad.

KM.name: Comoros
KM.headline: Illegal; criminal penalties
KM.law: Cannabis is a prohibited narcotic under Comorian law. Possession, use, cultivation and sale are crimes. Comoros has not carried out executions since 1997, and HRI does not list it as a drug death-penalty state.
KM.punishment: Possession and trafficking both carry prison terms and fines; exact ranges not verified.
KM.access: No legal access. No medical program.
KM.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.

KN.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
KN.headline: Private adult use protected by court; up to 56 g allowed
KN.law: 2019 High Court ruling (Ventose J.) held blanket bans on private adult use, possession and cultivation unconstitutional. Cannabis Act 2020 set limits of 56 g (15 g resin) for adults 18+ in private; public use and sale remain illegal.
KN.punishment: Within limits in private: no penalty. Public use or over the limit: ticket or charges. Trafficking/sale: criminal, with prison (formerly 5 yrs to life for large amounts).
KN.access: Home grow in a secured private area; no licensed retail. Medicinal Cannabis Authority set up under 2020 law; operating status unclear.
KN.tourists: Private possession tolerated within limits; no legal place to buy.
KN.home_grow: Allowed in secured private area (limit reported 4–5 plants)
KN.medical: Medicinal Cannabis Authority created 2020; licences not confirmed

KP.name: North Korea
KP.headline: Illegal despite 'weed is legal' myth; drug crimes harshly punished
KP.law: Drug possession, use and trafficking are crimes under the Criminal Code. Reports that cannabis is legal or unregulated are unverified folklore; wild hemp is grown for fibre. No public, verifiable statute on cannabis specifically.
KP.punishment: Drug offences draw labour camp terms; drug-related public executions are reported by defectors (mostly meth). Specific cannabis penalties unknown.
KP.access: No legal access. Foreign visitors travel only on supervised tours.
KP.tourists: No. Bringing any drugs risks arrest; tourists are closely monitored.
KP.death_detail: Drug death penalty exists; cannabis coverage unconfirmed.

KR.name: South Korea
KR.headline: Illegal; the law allows death for trafficking, but no death sentence for marijuana is documented
KR.law: Narcotics Control Act bans cannabis use, possession, cultivation and sale. Since 2019 only government-approved cannabis-derived medicines (e.g. Epidiolex) are allowed, imported via a state agency on prescription.
KR.punishment: Use/possession: up to 5 yrs or fine up to ₩50M. Import/export: 5 yrs–life. For-profit or habitual import/export (Art. 58(2)): death, life or ≥10 yrs. Moratorium: no executions since Dec 1997.
KR.access: No recreational access. Patients can get approved cannabis-derived drugs (Epidiolex, Sativex etc.) via the Korea Orphan & Essential Drug Center with a prescription.
KR.tourists: No. Korea prosecutes its citizens for cannabis use abroad; visitors are arrested.
KR.medical: Limited: approved cannabis-derived medicines only, since 2019. No flower.
KR.death_detail: Art. 58(2): for-profit/habitual cannabis import/export → death possible. Symbolic: no executions since 1997.

KW.name: Kuwait
KW.headline: Illegal; Dec 2025 law widened death penalty for trafficking
KW.law: All use, possession and trade banned. Decree-Law 159 of 2025 (in force mid-Dec 2025) replaced the 1983/1987 laws, adding random testing and treatment immunity for self-referral.
KW.punishment: Use/possession: prison and fines (refusing a test: up to 4 years); foreigners deported. Trafficking: death or life plus KD 100,000-2m fines. 2 drug executions in 2025 (HRI).
KW.tourists: No. Illegal for everyone; foreigners also face deportation.
KW.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: Jul 2022: Criminal Court sentenced an Indian expatriate to death for importing 1.25 kg hashish in chocolate boxes; Apr 2026 appeal court upheld death for 3 Iranians over 120+ kg hashish (plus pills). Death for trafficking, cultivation for trade or aggravated cases (Decree-Law 159/2025). 2 drug executions in 2025 (HRI).

KZ.name: Kazakhstan
KZ.headline: Illegal; small amounts fined, larger amounts and dealing are crimes
KZ.law: Criminal Code art. 296 (possession without intent to sell) and 297 (trafficking) ban cannabis, which grows wild in the Chuy Valley. Small amounts are an administrative offence; government schedules set the gram thresholds.
KZ.punishment: Small personal amounts: administrative fine or short arrest. Larger possession: fines, restricted freedom or prison. Trafficking: long prison terms, up to life in especially large/organised cases.

LA.name: Laos
LA.headline: Illegal; under 5 g treated as a user, trafficking up to life
LA.law: Penal Code 2017 (Arts. 318, 320) bans cannabis cultivation, sale, transport and possession. Users holding under 5 g are classed as 'victims' sent to treatment. Cannabis 'happy' menus in tourist towns are illegal, not tolerated by law.
LA.punishment: Under 5 g: treatment. 5–10 g: 6 mo–2 yrs + fine. Sale: <5 kg 6 mo–3 yrs; 5–10 kg 3–7 yrs; >10 kg/organised 5–10 yrs. THC/hashish >500 g: life.
LA.access: No legal access. No medical program (CBD reform discussed, not enacted).
LA.tourists: No. Foreigners are fined, jailed or deported; police sting operations reported.
LA.death_detail: Death exists for heroin/meth etc.; Penal Code caps cannabis at life (THC/hashish >500 g). No executions since 1989.

LB.name: Lebanon
LB.headline: Illegal to use; 2020 law allows licensed medical farming, not yet running
LB.law: Use, possession and sale are crimes under Law 673 of 1998. Law 178 of 2020 legalized licensed cultivation for medical/industrial use; its regulator was only formed in July 2025 and no licences were reported issued as of mid-2026.
LB.punishment: Personal use: 3 months-3 years' prison plus fine; treatment can replace prosecution. Trafficking/cultivation: hard labour, long terms (years to life) and heavy fines.
LB.access: No legal access for consumers. Licensed medical/industrial cultivation exists in law (2020) but no patient program operates yet.
LB.tourists: No. Visitors face the same penalties.
LB.medical: Law 178/2020 permits medical cultivation; no patient program yet

LC.name: Saint Lucia
LC.headline: Up to 30 g is not an offence since 2021; no legal sales
LC.law: Drugs (Prevention of Misuse) Act s.8A (Act 13 of 2021, in force Sept 2021): possessing 30 g or less of cannabis or resin is not an offence. Selling, trafficking and public use remain illegal; a regulated cannabis industry bill is still being drafted.
LC.punishment: Up to 30 g: no penalty. Over 30 g, cultivation for sale or trafficking: criminal charges with fines and prison.
LC.access: No licensed shops, dispensaries or medical program as of late 2025.
LC.tourists: Up to 30 g not an offence; no legal place to buy.

LI.name: Liechtenstein
LI.headline: Illegal; follows Swiss-style rules incl. legal low-THC (under 1%) hemp
LI.law: Cannabis with 1% THC or more is a narcotic under the Narcotics Act (BMG 1983, amended). Possession, use, cultivation and sale are offences. Low-THC CBD hemp (under 1%) is legal, mirroring Swiss rules. No legalisation plans.
LI.punishment: Use, or possession/cultivation for own use: a contravention (Übertretung) with a fine up to CHF 50,000 (prison up to 6 months only if unpaid); minor cases may go unpunished (BMG art. 21). Unauthorised cultivation, possession, sale or transport: up to 3 years or a day-fine; serious cases (large quantity, gang, commercial) 1-20 years (art. 20).
LI.access: No legal access. Cannabinoid medicines (e.g. Sativex) may be available by prescription; no formal medical program found.
LI.tourists: No legal purchase or use (CBD under 1% THC only).
LI.medical: No program; the Office of Public Health may grant exceptional permits for limited medical use of cannabis with 1% THC or more (BMG art. 6(4)); approved cannabinoid medicines possibly prescribable

LK.name: Sri Lanka
LK.headline: Illegal; drug death penalty exists but not for cannabis
LK.law: Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance (1929, amended 1984) bans possession, sale and cultivation of cannabis. Licensed cannabis is used in traditional Ayurvedic medicine under the Ayurveda Act.
LK.punishment: Cannabis: under 1 kg Rs20,000-50,000 and/or 1-2 yrs; 1-5 kg 2-5 yrs; 5-100 kg 5-10 yrs; 100 kg+ 10-15 yrs (fines up to Rs500,000). Small amounts can also be dealt with by a magistrate.
LK.access: No recreational access. Ayurvedic practitioners can obtain cannabis-based traditional medicines through state-licensed channels.
LK.medical: Ayurvedic cannabis preparations under state licence; no modern medical program.
LK.death_detail: Death/life applies to heroin, cocaine, morphine, meth (5 g+) and opium (1 kg+); cannabis tiers top out at 15 years.

LR.name: Liberia
LR.headline: Illegal; trafficking non-bailable since 2023 drug law
LR.law: Controlled Drugs and Substances Act 2014, amended and renamed the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act of 2023: cannabis use, possession and sale are crimes. 2023 law made trafficking non-bailable; use stays bailable.
LR.punishment: Use/possession: felony-level offence (bail set at twice drug value); prison possible. Trafficking: non-bailable first-degree felony, 10+ years prison. Exact final ranges not fully verified.
LR.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
LR.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

LS.name: Lesotho
LS.headline: Illegal for adults; Africa's first medical cannabis licences (2017)
LS.law: The Drugs of Abuse Act 2008 and the 2018 cannabis regulations let the Health Ministry license medical cannabis cultivation; Lesotho was Africa's first to license it, in 2017. Recreational use, possession and sale stay illegal.
LS.punishment: Recreational possession and trafficking are crimes under the Drugs of Abuse Act 2008 (fines and prison); exact ranges not verified.
LS.access: No personal access. Licensed export growers only (licences cost about EUR 30,000/yr); no domestic patient market.
LS.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.
LS.medical: Licensed medical cultivation since 2017, mainly export

LT.name: Lithuania
LT.headline: Medical law since 2019 but no patients served; any possession is a crime
LT.law: Since 1 May 2019 registered cannabis medicines may be sold in pharmacies, but no products are authorised and no patients treated (2025). Possessing even small amounts is a crime; decriminalisation bills failed (2022).
