LT.punishment: Small amount, no intent to sell: community service, fine, restriction of liberty or arrest. Larger amounts: up to 2 yrs. Trafficking: 2-8 yrs; up to 15 yrs for very large amounts.
LT.access: No practical legal access: framework exists, no authorised products. No shops or home grow.
LT.medical: Legal since 2019 on paper; no authorised products or patients yet

LU.name: Luxembourg
LU.headline: Private possession allowed; possession or use in public is fined
LU.law: Since 21 Jul 2023, adults may grow up to 4 plants per household at their residence and use cannabis at home. Public use and sale remain illegal. Public possession of up to 3 g is a minor offence. Planned state-regulated sales have not been introduced.
LU.punishment: Public possession up to 3 g: fine €25-500 (on-the-spot €145). Over 3 g: 8 days to 6 months and/or €251-2,500. Sale/trafficking: 1 to 5 years plus heavy fines, more if aggravated.
LU.access: Home grow only: no shops or clubs. Seeds can be bought legally. Medical: doctor's prescription, dispensed free through hospital pharmacies.
LU.tourists: No legal purchase; home grow rights apply to residents.
LU.possession_limit: 4 plants' yield at home; 3 g public = fine

LV.name: Latvia
LV.headline: Illegal; first small-amount offence is a fine, repeat within a year is a crime
LV.law: First-time use or possession of a small amount (about 1 g) is an administrative offence; repeat within 12 months, or larger amounts, is criminal. No medical program (2025 push by Progressives not enacted). Sale and grow are crimes.
LV.punishment: First small amount: warning or fine up to about EUR 280-350. Repeat: 15 days-3 months jail, community service or fine. Larger amounts: up to 3 yrs. Trafficking: 2-15 yrs.
LV.access: No legal access. No medical program.
LV.medical: No program; legalisation of medical cannabis under debate

LY.name: Libya
LY.headline: Strictly illegal; death possible for trafficking in law
LY.law: All use, possession and trade banned under Law No. 7 of 1990 on narcotics. Enforcement uneven amid divided government.
LY.punishment: Personal use: prison plus fine. Trafficking: life prison; law allows death. 1+ drug death sentence in 2025 (HRI).
LY.tourists: No. Visitors face the same penalties.
LY.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: Aug 2019: Benghazi Criminal Court sentenced 4 Syrians to death by firing squad for smuggling a huge quantity of hashish hidden in container floors via Benghazi port. Death or life for trafficking/import/cultivation of cannabis (Table 5) and other narcotics (Law 7/1990 art.34, as amended by Law 23/2002); death mandatory if aggravated. 1+ drug death sentence in 2025 (HRI).
LY.subnational: Rival governments in Tripoli and the east; same 1990 law, inconsistent enforcement.

MA.name: Morocco
MA.headline: Legal medical/industrial cannabis; recreational use still a crime
MA.law: Law 13-21 (2021) legalized licensed cultivation for medical, cosmetic and industrial use under regulator ANRAC; first legal harvest 2023. Recreational use, possession and sale remain crimes (1974 dahir).
MA.punishment: Personal use: 2 months-1 year's prison and/or MAD 500-5,000 fine. Trafficking: 5-10 years plus heavy fines.
MA.access: Limited: 141 registered products (mostly cosmetics/supplements, 1 drug) at 600+ authorised outlets; THC medicine by prescription only. No recreational access.
MA.tourists: No recreational purchase or use; only legal registered products.
MA.medical: Yes: legal medical cannabis framework (Law 13-21), small product range
MA.subnational: Legal cultivation limited to licensed farmers in Al Hoceima, Chefchaouen and Taounate provinces.

MC.name: Monaco
MC.headline: Fully illegal, including for medical use
MC.law: Production, sale, possession and use of cannabis are criminal offences in Monaco. No medical program and no decriminalisation.
MC.punishment: Use or possession for personal use: 6 months to 3 years' prison and/or a fine (Loi 890 art. 5). Cultivation, possession, sale, purchase, transport: 5-10 years plus fine (art. 2); group use is punished the same. Production, import/export: 10-20 years (art. 2-1). Penalties doubled near schools/minors; foreigners can be banned from Monaco.
MC.tourists: No legal purchase or use; French rules apply next door.

MD.name: Moldova
MD.headline: Small amounts an administrative offence; no medical; tougher bill pending
MD.law: Possessing small amounts (about 2 g dried) without intent to sell is a contravention, not a crime; larger amounts and cultivation are crimes. No medical program. A 2026 bill to raise fines/penalties passed first reading.
MD.punishment: Small amounts: fine (about MDL 1,500-3,000) or community service. Larger possession: criminal. Trafficking: roughly 2-15 yrs depending on quantity.
MD.access: No legal access. No medical program.
MD.tourists: No legal purchase; possession risks fines.
MD.subnational: Breakaway Transnistria is outside Moldovan government control and applies its own rules.

ME.name: Montenegro
ME.headline: Possession for own use is a misdemeanour (fine); dealing is a crime; no medical
ME.law: Under the Law on Prevention of Drug Abuse, possessing drugs for personal use is a misdemeanour, not a crime. Production and sale are crimes under the Criminal Code. No medical cannabis program.
ME.punishment: Personal possession: misdemeanour fine (roughly EUR 150-2,000). Production/sale: 2-10 yrs; more for organised or large-scale trafficking.
ME.access: No legal access. No medical program.
ME.tourists: No legal purchase; possession risks a fine.

MG.name: Madagascar
MG.headline: Illegal; harsh prison terms, widely grown
MG.law: Law 97-039 (1997) on narcotics bans using, possessing, growing and trafficking cannabis (rongony), although it is widely grown and consumed.
MG.punishment: Use or possession: prison plus fines (reports range from 2 months-5 years to 2-10 years). Production or trafficking: 5-20 years' forced labour and large fines (reported).
MG.access: No legal access. No medical program.
MG.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.

MH.name: Marshall Islands
MH.headline: Illegal; 2025 amendment explicitly lists marijuana as prohibited
MH.law: Cannabis is illegal under the Prohibited Drugs Act 1987; a 2025 amendment added marijuana and marijuana concentrate to the definition of prohibited drug. Possession, cultivation and sale are criminal.
MH.punishment: Possession and trafficking are criminal offences carrying prison and fines; exact current maximums not confirmed.
MH.access: No legal access. A prescription exception exists on paper, but no medical cannabis is available.

MK.name: North Macedonia
MK.headline: Medical cannabis oils/extracts by prescription since 2016; recreational illegal
MK.law: 2016 amendments allow medical cannabis products (oils, extracts) on prescription; licensed companies grow mainly for export. Recreational possession, cultivation and sale are crimes.
MK.punishment: Personal possession: criminal; small amounts usually a fine or up to 1 yr. Production and trafficking: 3-10 yrs, more if organised.
MK.access: Medical only: specialist prescription for cannabis oils/extracts at pharmacies; domestic patient access remains limited. No shops or home grow.
MK.medical: Yes since 2016: prescription oils/extracts; flower export-focused industry

ML.name: Mali
ML.headline: Illegal; use and trafficking are criminal
ML.law: Law 01-078 (2001) on drug control bans cultivation, possession, use and trafficking of cannabis. No medical or hemp program.
ML.punishment: Use/possession: prison and fines. Trafficking: long prison terms and heavy fines. Exact current ranges not verified.
ML.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
ML.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.
ML.subnational: State control is weak in northern/central regions, but national law applies everywhere.

MM.name: Myanmar
MM.headline: Illegal; the law allows death for trafficking, but no death sentence for marijuana is documented
MM.law: 1993 Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Law (amended 2018) defines the cannabis plant as a narcotic drug. The 2018 amendment shifted users toward registration/treatment; cultivation, sale and import/export remain serious crimes.
MM.punishment: Cultivation: 5–10 yrs. Possession ≥100 g is presumed for sale: 10 yrs–life. Production, sale, import/export (s.20): 15 yrs–life or death. Personal-use penalties vary; treatment favoured since 2018.
MM.access: No legal access. No medical program.
MM.tourists: No. Visitors face the same law; avoid entirely.
MM.death_detail: s.20 allows death for producing/selling/importing narcotic drugs incl. cannabis. No drug executions in decades (HRI: symbolic).
MM.subnational: Large areas are under armed-group control, where state law is not enforced.

MN.name: Mongolia
MN.headline: Illegal; small amounts may draw fines, trafficking means prison
MN.law: Cannabis (wild-growing across the steppe) is banned under the Law on Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances and the Criminal Code. Use, possession, cultivation and sale are prohibited. A tougher draft drug law was in early stages in 2025.
MN.punishment: Small personal amounts: administrative fines or short detention reported; larger amounts: criminal charges, years in prison. Trafficking: long prison terms. Thresholds and exact ranges unverified from primary text.
MN.access: No legal access. No medical program.
MN.tourists: No. Same law applies to visitors.
MN.death_detail: Mongolia abolished the death penalty for all crimes in 2017.

MR.name: Mauritania
MR.headline: Strictly illegal; death possible for repeat 'high-risk drug' trafficking
MR.law: Law 93-37 (1993) bans production, trafficking and use of narcotics. Use is a crime. Penalties split by schedule: 'high-risk drugs' (Tables I-II) vs 'risk drugs' (Table III), assigned by ministerial order.
MR.punishment: Use: up to 2 years and/or 50,000-100,000 UM fine. High-risk drug trafficking: 15-30 years plus 10M-100M UM fine; death for a repeat offence. A 2016 cannabis-resin trafficking case drew 15 years.
MR.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
MR.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.
MR.death_detail: Death for a repeat offence of producing, importing or trafficking 'high-risk drugs' (Law 93-37 arts.3-5). Cannabis resin is treated as high-risk in practice (2016 case: 15 yrs imposed, 30 sought). HRI: symbolic.

MT.name: Malta
MT.headline: First EU country to legalise (2021): 7 g, 4 plants, licensed clubs
MT.law: Since Dec 2021 adults may possess up to 7 g in public and 50 g of home-grown at home, grow 4 plants per household, and buy from licensed non-profit associations regulated by ARUC. Commercial sale and public use remain illegal.
MT.punishment: 7-28 g: fine €50-100. Public use: fine (about €235); near minors €300-500. Since Bill 128 (passed 16 May 2025), cannabis offences go to the Court of Magistrates instead of the Commissioner for Justice; a strong cannabis smell in public draws €50-100, and smell leaving a property up to €235.
MT.access: Licensed non-profit associations (ARUC): max 500 members, residents only, 7 g/day and 50 g/month. Only a few dozen operate. Home grow (4 plants). Medical: prescription via pharmacies since 2018.
MT.tourists: Clubs are residents-only; no legal source for visitors.
MT.medical: Since 2018: doctor's prescription, dispensed at pharmacies

MU.name: Mauritius
MU.headline: Illegal and punished severely; medical route on paper only
MU.law: The Dangerous Drugs Act 2000 treats cannabis (gandia) severely. A 2022 amendment allows Health Ministry-authorised medical cannabis, but no working program exists. A 2025 decriminalisation proposal from NGOs has not been adopted.
MU.punishment: Possession and use: fines and prison; most drug prisoners are held for small amounts of cannabis. Trafficking: decades of penal servitude possible; exact ranges not verified.
MU.access: No legal access. Medical use needs Ministry authorisation under the 2022 amendment, but it is not operational.
MU.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.
MU.medical: 2022 amendment permits authorised use; not operational

MV.name: Maldives
MV.headline: Illegal; the law allows death for trafficking, but no death sentence for marijuana is documented
MV.law: Drugs Act 17/2011 bans cannabis. Act 28/2025 (3rd amendment, ratified 6 Dec 2025, in force March 2026) made death the penalty for importing over 350 g of cannabis on entry, and life without parole for traffickers.
MV.punishment: Small amounts for use: diversion to treatment or imprisonment and fines. Trafficking: life imprisonment, no parole or plea deals. Importing 350 g+ cannabis: death, only by unanimous Supreme Court bench.
MV.tourists: No. Resort islands enforce the same law; airport customs searches are strict.
MV.death_detail: Since 7 Mar 2026: death for importing over 350 g cannabis on entry; needs unanimous Supreme Court, otherwise life + fine. No execution since 1953; HRI: symbolic.

MW.name: Malawi
MW.headline: Illegal for adults; licensed medical and hemp industry since 2020
MW.law: The Cannabis Regulation Act 2020 created a Cannabis Regulatory Authority that licenses hemp and medicinal cannabis cultivation, processing and export. Recreational use and possession stay illegal under the Dangerous Drugs Act.
MW.punishment: Possession and trafficking both carry prison terms and fines under the Dangerous Drugs Act; exact ranges not verified.
MW.access: No personal access. Licensed farms and processors (hemp and medicinal) only; little or no domestic patient access.
MW.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.
MW.medical: Licensed medicinal/hemp industry (2020 Act); patient access limited

MX.name: Mexico
MX.headline: Small amounts not prosecuted; court-backed grow permits; no legal sales
MX.law: COFEPRIS issues personal self-consumption permits to grow and possess; in July 2026 the Supreme Court upheld a single collective permit (issued in 2022 to nine named holders), so joint permits are valid if every holder is named.
MX.punishment: Above 5 g or without a permit: prosecution possible, up to 3 yrs for possession beyond the threshold. Sale/trafficking (narcomenudeo and federal): about 4–8 yrs for small-scale dealing, 10–25 yrs for federal trafficking.
MX.access: Hard: no shops. Adults can apply to COFEPRIS for a self-consumption permit (often via amparo). Medical cannabis legal since 2017; 2021 regulations allow prescribed products.
MX.tourists: No legal purchase; carrying under 5 g is not prosecuted but police shakedowns are common.
MX.home_grow: Only with a COFEPRIS self-consumption permit
MX.medical: Legal since 2017; 2021 regulations; prescription products, limited availability

MY.name: Malaysia
MY.headline: Illegal; trafficking ≥200 g can still mean death (discretionary since 2023)
MY.law: Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 bans use, possession, cultivation and sale. Holding ≥200 g cannabis is presumed trafficking (s.39B). 2023 reform ended the mandatory death penalty; judges now choose. Study on full abolition began 2026.
MY.punishment: Possession: up to 5 yrs and/or RM100,000. Use: up to 2 yrs or RM5,000. Trafficking (≥200 g): death, or 30–40 yrs + ≥12 strokes of the cane. Cultivation: up to life + caning. No executions since 2018 moratorium.
MY.access: No recreational access. Law allows registering cannabis-based medicines with the Drug Control Authority, but none is currently registered.
MY.tourists: No. Visitors face the same law, including caning.
MY.medical: Registration route exists in law; no cannabis medicine registered.
MY.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: Nov 2021: Johor Baru High Court sentenced a food delivery rider to death for trafficking 764.9 g of cannabis (reduced on appeal, 2023) Discretionary death for trafficking ≥200 g (s.39B). 9+ drug death sentences in 2025; executions halted since 2018.

MZ.name: Mozambique
MZ.headline: Illegal; drug use is a crime, but courts may substitute fines
MZ.law: Law 3/97 makes using, possessing, growing and selling cannabis (suruma) crimes. Reform groups are pushing to decriminalise use, but no change has been enacted.
MZ.punishment: Use: up to 2 years in prison, which courts may replace with fines, community service or a waiver. Trafficking: long prison terms (8-12 years reported; not verified).
MZ.access: No legal access. No medical program.
MZ.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.

NA.name: Namibia
NA.headline: Illegal; court bids to legalise it failed in 2026
NA.law: The 1971 Abuse of Dependence-Producing Substances Act bans possession, use and dealing. In 2026 the High Court rejected two challenges and deferred to an ongoing Law Reform Commission review.
NA.punishment: Possession: fine and/or prison. Holding over 115 g is presumed to be dealing (upheld in Feb 2026), and dealing carries heavier prison terms; exact ranges not verified.
NA.access: No legal access. No medical program.
NA.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.

NE.name: Niger
NE.headline: Illegal; use and trafficking are criminal
NE.law: Ordinance 99-42 (1999) on drug control bans cultivation, possession, use and trafficking of cannabis. Niger is a transit route for Moroccan cannabis resin. No medical program.
NE.punishment: Use/possession: prison and fines. Trafficking: long prison terms and heavy fines. Exact current ranges not verified.
NE.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
NE.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

NG.name: Nigeria
NG.headline: Illegal; dealing can bring life in prison; death penalty bill dropped
NG.law: NDLEA Act (1989, Cap N30) bans growing, possessing, using and dealing 'Indian hemp'. 2024 Senate push for death for traffickers was dropped; conference version kept life imprisonment. Legalisation bills stalled (2023).
NG.punishment: Possession: statute sets 15-25 years, though courts often give 2-4 years for small amounts. Dealing/cultivation: up to life imprisonment (16 years given for 407 g in 2025).
NG.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
NG.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.
NG.medical: None; 2021/2023 medical cannabis bills stalled in the House
NG.death_detail: No drug death penalty. 2024 bill to add it was replaced by life imprisonment; HRI: not adopted as of Feb 2026.
NG.subnational: Federal law applies everywhere; state Sharia codes in the north also ban intoxicants.

NI.name: Nicaragua
NI.headline: Illegal; small amounts get fines and community service, more means prison
NI.law: Penal Code (Law 641, 2008) and Law 735 (2010) ban possession, cultivation and sale. Under 5 g is a minor offence; above 5 g is a crime. Trafficking offences are classed as organized crime.
NI.punishment: Under 5 g: day-fines plus 30-60 days community service. 5-20 g: 6 months-3 years prison; over 20 g: 3-8 years. Trafficking: 5-15 years domestic, 10-20 years international; cultivation 5-10 years.
NI.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis program.

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.headline: Tolerated: coffeeshops sell up to 5 g; growing and wholesale still illegal
NL.law: Cannabis is illegal under the Opium Act, but a toleration policy (since 1976) lets licensed coffeeshops sell up to 5 g per person per day to adults; possession up to 5 g is not prosecuted. A legal-supply experiment runs in 10 cities since Apr 2025.
NL.punishment: Up to 5 g: no prosecution (police may confiscate). Possession up to 30 g: max 1 month or fine; over 30 g: up to 2 years. Dealing/cultivation: up to 4 years, more for large-scale or organised grows.
NL.access: Very easy: about 550 coffeeshops; 18+, ID, 5 g per day. In 10 experiment cities shops sell only state-licensed product. Medical cannabis from pharmacies on prescription.
NL.tourists: Allowed in most cities incl. Amsterdam; some border towns (e.g. Maastricht) are residents-only.
NL.home_grow: Up to 5 plants tolerated (may still be removed)
NL.medical: Since 2003: prescription, pharmacy-dispensed (Office of Medicinal Cannabis)
NL.subnational: Municipalities decide whether to allow coffeeshops; many have none; some southern towns ban non-residents.

NO.name: Norway
NO.headline: Illegal; small amounts usually fined; prescriptions possible; medical by prescription
NO.law: Possession and use are offences under the Medicines Act; sale under the Penal Code. A 2021 decriminalisation bill failed (2022), but 2022 prosecutor guidance spares people with addiction from punishment for small amounts. Specialists may prescribe medical cannabis.
NO.punishment: Possession (up to about 15 g): usually a fine or a conditional waiver with drug follow-up; legal max 6 months. Trafficking: up to 2 years (minor), 10 years, or up to 15-21 years if aggravated.
NO.access: No recreational access. Medical: specialist prescription of approved products (Sativex, Epidiolex) or imported flower with Norwegian Medicines Agency approval; uptake is low.
NO.medical: Specialist prescription; flower requires agency approval

NP.name: Nepal
NP.headline: Illegal nationally since 1976; Gandaki province legalised medical farming 2026
NP.law: Narcotic Drugs (Control) Act 1976 bans cultivation, possession, sale and use of cannabis (ended the legal hashish shops of the hippie era). A federal bill to allow regulated production is pending. Gandaki Province passed a medical/industrial cultivation law in July 2026.
NP.punishment: Personal use/possession: up to about one month in jail and/or a fine. Cultivation and trafficking: multi-year prison terms and fines, rising with quantity.
NP.access: No recreational access. Gandaki Province (Aug 2026) permits licensed, monitored cultivation of <3% THC cannabis for medical/industrial use only; no retail sales.
NP.medical: Provincial medical/industrial cultivation law in Gandaki (2026); no national program.
NP.subnational: Gandaki Province allows licensed medical/industrial cultivation since Aug 2026, despite the national ban.

NR.name: Nauru
NR.headline: Illegal; no legal or medical access
NR.law: Cannabis is a prohibited drug under Nauru's illicit drugs legislation; possession, cultivation, import and sale are criminal offences.
NR.punishment: Possession and trafficking carry prison terms and fines; exact current maximums not confirmed.
NR.access: No legal access. No medical program.

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.headline: Recreational illegal (2020 referendum failed); medicinal scheme since 2020
NZ.law: Cannabis is a Class C drug under the Misuse of Drugs Act 1975; possession, cultivation and supply are offences. 2019 amendment told police to prefer health/diversion over prosecution for personal use. 2020 legalisation referendum failed (48.8% yes).
NZ.punishment: Possession: max 3 months jail and/or NZ$500 fine, presumption against jail; often warning/diversion. Possession over 28 g presumes supply. Cultivation up to 7 yrs; dealing/supply up to 8 yrs.
NZ.access: Medicinal Cannabis Scheme (April 2020): any NZ registered doctor can prescribe approved products, incl. dried flower; moderately accessible via specialist clinics. No home grow, no retail.
NZ.tourists: No legal purchase or use without a NZ prescription.
NZ.medical: Medicinal Cannabis Scheme since 1 April 2020; prescription via NZ doctors

OM.name: Oman
OM.headline: Strictly illegal; long prison terms, death possible for trafficking in law
OM.law: All use, possession and trade banned under the Law on Combating Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Royal Decree 67/2026, issued 3 Sep 2026, Official Gazette 1664 of 6 Sep 2026), which repealed Royal Decree 17/99.
OM.punishment: Personal use: 1-3 years' prison + RO 1,000-5,000 fine (treatment possible); foreigners deported. Trafficking: import/production RO 35,000-60,000 fine + prison; possession/sale for trafficking at least 15 years; death for smuggling-for-trafficking in aggravated cases (repeat offence, abuse of office, using incapacitated persons, intl gangs).
OM.tourists: No. Illegal for everyone; foreigners also face deportation.
OM.death_detail: Death for aggravated drug smuggling for trafficking under RD 67/2026; press reports show no carve-out by substance, so it appears to cover cannabis too (law text not yet published online). Earlier RD 17/99 art.43 also allowed death.

PA.name: Panama
PA.headline: Recreational illegal; medical law (2021) is slowly reaching pharmacies
PA.law: Recreational use, possession and sale are crimes under the 2007 Penal Code. Law 242 (2021) legalized medical and therapeutic cannabis; 7 producer licences issued Jan 2024; THC was added to the controlled-medicines list Oct 2025.
PA.punishment: Simple possession for personal use is penalized (Art. 321); possession in circumstances showing it is not for consumption: 5-10 years. Trafficking (Art. 313): 8-15 years prison.
PA.access: Medical only: prescription products at licensed pharmacies, CBD first with THC products phased in; no home delivery or online sales. No recreational access.
PA.medical: Law 242 (2021); pharmacy sales starting 2025-26, limited range

PE.name: Peru
PE.headline: Up to 8 g for personal use not punishable; medical law since 2017
PE.law: Penal Code Art. 299: possession for immediate personal use is not punished up to 8 g of cannabis (2 g of derivatives), one drug at a time. Sale and growing are crimes. Medical: Law 30681 (2017); Law 31312 (2021) lets patient associations grow.
PE.punishment: Within 8 g: no penalty. Micro-commercialization (Art. 298): 3-7 years. Trafficking (Art. 296): 8-15 years prison.
PE.access: No recreational sales. Medical: registered patients buy prescription products (mostly imported) at pharmacies; local cultivation licences exist on paper (DS 004-2023-SA).
PE.tourists: Can carry up to 8 g for personal use; no legal place to buy.
PE.medical: Legal since 2017; patient registry, pharmacy products

PG.name: Papua New Guinea
PG.headline: Illegal; widely grown but no legal or medical access
PG.law: Cannabis is prohibited for all purposes. Possession, cultivation and sale are criminal offences (Dangerous Drugs Act 1952; Controlled Substances Act 2021 toughened drug penalties). Medical cannabis bills proposed 2019-2020 never enacted.
PG.punishment: Possession: jail and/or fine (reported up to 2 yrs or K5,000). Cultivation and sale: long prison terms (reported 15-20 yrs); Controlled Substances Act allows life or K2m for trafficking.
PG.access: No legal access. No medical program; no cannabinoid medicines registered.
PG.medical: None; medical cannabis bills proposed 2019-2020, not enacted

PH.name: Philippines
PH.headline: Illegal; selling any amount means life imprisonment
PH.law: Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act 2002 (RA 9165) bans use, possession, cultivation and sale. Death penalty abolished 2006. A medical cannabis bill cleared House panels Feb 2026; not law.
PH.punishment: Use: 6 months rehab (first offence). Possession <300 g: 12–20 yrs; 300–500 g: 20 yrs–life; ≥500 g: life. Sale or cultivation: life imprisonment + fine ₱500,000–10M.
PH.access: No legal access. Only FDA compassionate permits for imported CBD medicines (e.g. for epilepsy).
PH.tourists: No. Same penalties apply to visitors.
PH.medical: No program; FDA compassionate special permits for CBD drugs. Bill pending.
PH.death_detail: Abolished 2006 (RA 9346); life imprisonment is max. Reinstatement bills pending.

PK.name: Pakistan
PK.headline: Illegal for adults; drug death penalty abolished; medical/hemp regulator set up
PK.law: Control of Narcotic Substances Act 1997 bans possession, sale and cultivation of cannabis/charas. Death penalty for drug offences removed by the CNSA (Amendment) Act 2023 (passed by joint sitting of Parliament 25 July 2023, effective immediately); the Sept 2022 amendment had retained death. 2024 ordinance created a Cannabis Control and Regulatory Authority (CCRA) for medical/industrial use.
PK.punishment: Small amounts: prison (up to a few years) and/or fines, scaled by quantity under CNSA s.9. Large-quantity trafficking: up to life imprisonment (replaced death in 2023). Courts lenient for tiny amounts but arrests common.
PK.access: No recreational access. CCRA licenses medical/industrial cannabis and hemp businesses (SECP-CCRA registration rules Oct 2026); no patient-facing dispensary system yet.
PK.medical: CCRA framework for medical/industrial cannabis; patient program not yet operational.
PK.death_detail: Abolished for drug offences by the July 2023 CNSA amendment (max now life). HRI still lists Pakistan because people remain on drug death row, and some courts kept imposing death after the amendment (JPP 2024).

PL.name: Poland
PL.headline: Medical cannabis in pharmacies since 2017; recreational possession is a crime
PL.law: Act on Counteracting Drug Addiction: possessing any amount is a criminal offence. Medical cannabis (dried flower, extracts) legal on prescription since 2017. Since Nov 2024 the first consultation must be in person (telehealth curbs). Sale and cultivation are crimes.
PL.punishment: Possession: up to 3 yrs prison (minor case: fine or up to 1 yr; prosecutors may drop small first-time cases). Supplying: 6 mo-8 yrs; significant quantity or for profit: up to 10-12 yrs.
PL.access: Medical only: doctor's prescription (first visit in person), filled at pharmacies. Large market, flower widely stocked. No shops, clubs or home grow.
PL.tourists: No. Possession is criminal; medical prescriptions only via Polish doctors.
PL.medical: Yes since 2017: prescription flower and extracts dispensed by pharmacies

PS.name: Palestine
PS.headline: Illegal in West Bank and Gaza; Gaza law allows death for trafficking
PS.law: West Bank: Decree-Law 18 of 2015 on narcotics bans use, possession, growing and sale. Gaza: a 2013 Hamas-era narcotics law, harsher. Israeli military law also applies in parts of the West Bank.
PS.punishment: West Bank: prison and fines for use; long terms for trafficking. Gaza: the 2013 law allows death for trafficking (HRI: insufficient data on use).
PS.tourists: No. Visitors face the same penalties.
PS.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: Gaza: Jan 2023 court sentenced a 30-year-old to hanging for possessing hashish with intent to traffic; Mar 2017 Hamas military court sentenced 2 to death (tramadol, marijuana, hashish). Gaza only: death or life for drug trafficking incl. hashish (Hamas-era Law 7/2013 art.29); a hashish trafficker was sentenced to death in March 2023. PA disputes the law's validity. West Bank: no death penalty.
PS.subnational: Gaza's 2013 narcotics law allows death for trafficking; West Bank law (2015) does not in practice; Area C settlers fall under Israeli law.

PT.name: Portugal
PT.headline: Decriminalised since 2001: up to 25 g is an administrative offence
PT.law: Since July 2001 (Law 30/2000), buying or possessing up to a 10-day supply (25 g herb, 5 g hash) for personal use is an administrative offence handled by health-led Dissuasion Commissions. A 2023 change made the threshold indicative. Sale and growing are crimes.
PT.punishment: Personal possession: referral to a Dissuasion Commission (warning, treatment, or small fine). Trafficking: 4-12 years; minor trafficking 1-5 years.
PT.access: No recreational access. Medical: since 2019 (Law 33/2018), doctors may prescribe Infarmed-authorised cannabis products, dispensed at pharmacies, when standard treatments fail.
PT.tourists: No legal purchase; same administrative rules apply to visitors.

PW.name: Palau
PW.headline: Illegal; medical cannabis bill proposed but not passed
PW.law: Marijuana is a Schedule I controlled substance in Palau; possession, cultivation and sale are criminal. A medical marijuana bill was introduced in the Olbiil Era Kelulau (2021-2023) but has not become law.
PW.punishment: Possession and sale are criminal offences with prison and fines; trafficking penalties severe. Exact current maximums not confirmed.
PW.access: No legal access. No medical program (bill pending/stalled).
PW.medical: None; medical marijuana bill introduced, not enacted

PY.name: Paraguay
PY.headline: Up to 10 g for personal use not punished; medical law exists but limited
PY.law: Law 1340/1988 Art. 30 exempts possession of up to 10 g of cannabis exclusively for personal use. Growing and sale are crimes. Law 6007/2017 allows medical cannabis products; patient home grow is not authorized (a 2020 bill was vetoed).
PY.punishment: Up to 10 g personal: no penalty. Unauthorized possession above that and trafficking: long prison terms (up to 15+ years under Law 1340). Even 2 plants have led to arrest.
PY.access: No recreational access. Medical: products from licensed local producers under Law 6007; access described as limited.
PY.tourists: Can carry up to 10 g personal; no legal place to buy.
PY.medical: Law 6007 (2017); licensed products, no patient grow

QA.name: Qatar
QA.headline: Strictly illegal; trafficking can carry death
QA.law: All use, possession and trade banned under Law No. 9 of 1987 on narcotics (amended).
QA.punishment: Personal use: prison plus fine; foreigners deported. Trafficking/import for sale: death or life (HRI: symbolic, no recent drug executions).
QA.tourists: No. Illegal for everyone; foreigners also face deportation.
QA.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: 2007: Doha court sentenced an Iranian to death in absentia over a 160 kg hashish smuggling attempt; 2013 and 2016 death sentences for hashish+opium sea smuggling. Law 9/1987 allows death for import/trafficking; no recent drug executions reported (HRI: symbolic).

RO.name: Romania
RO.headline: Medical allowed on paper since 2013 but no products; possession is a crime
RO.law: A 2013 amendment permits cannabis-derived medicines, but no products or licences have been authorised, so the program is non-operational. Law 143/2000 criminalises possession, cultivation and sale. A 3 g decriminalisation bill is pending.
RO.punishment: Possession for own use: 3 months-2 yrs prison or fine. Trafficking (risk drugs): 2-7 yrs; more for high-risk drugs or large scale.
RO.access: No practical legal access: medical framework exists but no authorised products. No shops or home grow.
RO.tourists: No. Even foreign prescriptions have been confiscated at the border.
RO.medical: Legal on paper (2013); non-operational, no licences or products

RS.name: Serbia
RS.headline: Illegal; no registered cannabis medicines; possession can mean prison
RS.law: Criminal Code and Law on Psychoactive Substances ban possession, cultivation and sale. A medical cannabis law has been promised for years but not passed; no cannabis medicines registered.
RS.punishment: Possession for personal use: up to 3 yrs (small amounts often fine or suspended). Trafficking: 3-12 yrs; more if organised.
RS.access: No legal access. No working medical program.
RS.medical: No program; medical use theoretical, no products registered

RU.name: Russia
RU.headline: Illegal; under 6 g means fine or up to 15 days jail, foreigners deported
RU.law: Possession up to 6 g dried is an administrative offence (Admin Code 6.8); above 6 g is criminal (CC Art. 228). Sale is a serious crime (Art. 228.1). Cultivation of under 20 plants is administrative; more is criminal. No medical program.
RU.punishment: Under 6 g: fine RUB 4,000-5,000 or up to 15 days arrest; foreigners expelled. 6-100 g: up to 3 yrs; over 100 g: 3-10 yrs. Sale: 4-8 yrs, up to 20 yrs or life for especially large amounts.
RU.access: No legal access. No medical program.
RU.tourists: No. Foreigners face arrest, deportation and re-entry ban; heavy sentences are common.

RW.name: Rwanda
RW.headline: Illegal for adults; harsh penalties; medical cannabis grown for export
RW.law: Penal Code (Law 68/2018, art. 263) criminalises using or dealing cannabis, which a 2019 ministerial order lists as a 'very severe' narcotic. Since 2021 the state licenses medical cannabis cultivation, for export only.
RW.punishment: Use: 1-2 years in prison or community service. Producing or selling 'very severe' narcotics such as cannabis: 20 years to life plus a fine of RWF 20-30 million.
RW.access: No legal access for individuals. Licensed firms grow medical cannabis for export only; no domestic patient access.
RW.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.
RW.medical: Licensed export cultivation (2021 rules); no domestic patients

SA.name: Saudi Arabia
SA.headline: Illegal; trafficking punished by death, 101 executions for cannabis-related crimes in 2025
SA.law: All use, possession and trade banned under the 2005 Narcotics Control Law and Sharia rulings (1987 fatwa sets death for drug smuggling).
SA.punishment: Personal use: 6 months-2 years' prison, possible flogging; foreigners deported. Trafficking: death. 240 drug executions in 2025, 101 for cannabis crimes, 188 foreigners (HRI).
SA.tourists: No. Visitors face prison, then deportation.
SA.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: Aug 2025: 4 Somalis + 3 Ethiopians executed in Najran for smuggling hashish (SPA); HRI 2025 counts 101 executions for cannabis-related crimes in 2025. Earlier: Iraqi Mattar al-Khazaali executed 2005 for hashish. Death for smuggling/trafficking. 2025: 240 drug executions, 101 cannabis-related, at least 1 for possession alone (HRI).

SB.name: Solomon Islands
SB.headline: Illegal; possession and growing prosecuted
SB.law: Cannabis is a prohibited plant under the Dangerous Drugs Act; possession, cultivation and supply are criminal offences. A Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Bill 2025 proposing much harsher penalties was still in committee in early 2026.
SB.punishment: Possession: up to SBD$5,000 fine and/or prison (case law cites 6 months to 3 yrs). Supply/trafficking: heavier terms; pending 2025 bill would allow life imprisonment.
SB.access: No legal access. No medical program.

SC.name: Seychelles
SC.headline: Illegal; 25 g or more is presumed trafficking
SC.law: The Misuse of Drugs Act 2016 bans buying, possessing, using, importing, growing and trafficking cannabis in any quantity. Possessing 25 g or more is presumed to be with intent to traffic.
SC.punishment: Possession: courts often impose suspended prison terms plus fines (e.g. SCR 10,000). Trafficking: longer prison terms; exact maximums not verified.
SC.access: No legal access. No medical program.
SC.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.

SD.name: Sudan
SD.headline: Illegal; the law allows death for trafficking, but no death sentence for marijuana is documented
SD.law: Cannabis (bango) is banned under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1994: use, possession, cultivation and sale are all crimes. Sudan is a major illicit grower (Darfur). The country has been at war since April 2023.
SD.punishment: Possession: prison and/or fines; exact ranges not verified. Trafficking: often life. Death is mandatory for aggravated trafficking or production (repeat offenders, officials, organised crime) under arts 15-17.
SD.access: No legal access. No medical program.
SD.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.
SD.death_detail: Death for aggravated trafficking or cultivation of any narcotic, explicitly including hashish/Indian hemp (1994 Act ss.3, 15(2), 17). HRI 2025: first drug death sentence reported.
SD.subnational: Law enforcement is fragmented by the civil war (army vs RSF areas).

SE.name: Sweden
SE.headline: Among Europe's strictest: even using cannabis is a crime; medical by prescription
SE.law: Under the Narcotic Drugs Penal Act, possession, use (criminal since 1988), cultivation and sale are crimes; police may drug-test suspects. Medical cannabis only via approved medicines or individual licences from the Medical Products Agency.
SE.punishment: Minor drug offence (small amount/use): fine or up to 6 months. Drug offence: up to 3 years. Serious: 2-7 years; particularly serious: 6-10 years.
SE.access: No recreational access. Medical: Sativex/Epidiolex, or flower via individual import licences (Läkemedelsverket); very few patients.
SE.tourists: No legal purchase or use; a positive drug test itself is an offence.
SE.medical: Very limited: approved medicines; individual licences for flower

SG.name: Singapore
SG.headline: Zero tolerance; over 500 g of cannabis means death (mandatory unless narrow courier exception applies)
SG.law: Misuse of Drugs Act: cannabis is Class A. Use, possession and sale are crimes. Possession of >15 g cannabis (30 g mixture, 10 g resin) is presumed trafficking. Citizens/PRs can be charged for use abroad.
SG.punishment: Use/possession: up to 10 yrs and/or S$20,000; repeat users 5+ yrs + caning. Trafficking: 5–20 yrs + 5–15 strokes. >500 g cannabis (>1 kg mixture, >200 g resin): mandatory death. 15 drug executions in 2025 (HRI).
SG.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis program.
SG.tourists: No. Arrivals can be urine-tested; citizens/PRs punished for use overseas.
SG.medical: None (rare case-by-case approval of cannabis-derived drugs only).
SG.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: Tangaraju Suppiah sentenced to death (2018) and hanged 26 Apr 2023 for abetting trafficking of 1,017.9 g cannabis; a second citizen hanged May 2023 for 1.5 kg cannabis. >500 g cannabis, >1 kg mixture or >200 g resin: death, mandatory unless the s.33B courier exception (life + caning) applies. 15 drug executions in 2025; cannabis cases hanged in recent years.

SI.name: Slovenia
SI.headline: Small possession is a fine-only offence; medical cannabis law in force Aug 2025
SI.law: Possessing a small amount for personal use is a misdemeanour, not a crime. Medical and Scientific Cannabis Act in force 20 Aug 2025: doctors may prescribe for any condition. A personal-use bill (home grow) is pending, not law. Sale and grow illegal.
SI.punishment: Personal possession: fine of roughly EUR 40-210, no criminal record. Trafficking: 1-10 yrs; up to 15 yrs if aggravated or organised.
SI.access: Medical: prescription (one-month supply, annual exam), filled at pharmacies; domestic licensed production. No shops, clubs or home grow.
SI.tourists: No legal purchase; possession risks a fine.
SI.medical: Yes since Aug 2025: prescription for any indication, pharmacies

SK.name: Slovakia
SK.headline: Fully illegal, including medical; possession of even small amounts is a crime
SK.law: Act 139/1998 and Criminal Code: cannabis is a Schedule 1 narcotic. Possession, cultivation and sale are crimes. No medical cannabis program; only CBD changes are under discussion (2026).
SK.punishment: Personal possession: up to 3 yrs (up to 3 doses), up to 5 yrs (larger personal amounts). Trafficking: 4-10 yrs, up to 25 yrs or life for large-scale or organised.
SK.access: No legal access. No medical program.
SK.medical: No program; growing, importing or selling medical cannabis not permitted

SL.name: Sierra Leone
SL.headline: Illegal; courts hand down very long sentences, even for grams
SL.law: National Drugs Control Act 2008: buying, selling, possessing or controlling any drug without authority is an offence (s.8). Kush crisis led to a 2024 public-health emergency; Act under review, no reform enacted.
SL.punishment: Possession: minimum 5 years. Courts have given 10 years for 60.5 g and 25 years for 30.5 g of kush (2025). Dealing/multiple counts: sentences of 30-40 years reported.
SL.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
SL.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

SM.name: San Marino
SM.headline: Recreational illegal; medical cannabis on prescription via State pharmacies (Law 113/2021)
SM.law: Recreational possession, use, cultivation and sale are illegal. In 2016 the government approved medical cannabis after a citizens' initiative; cannabinoid medicines (e.g. Sativex) are supplied through the public health service. A recreational initiative has not become law.
SM.punishment: Possession: criminal/administrative penalties under narcotics law (details unclear). Trafficking: prison (historically 3-8 years) plus fines.
SM.access: No recreational access. Medical: prescription cannabinoid medicines via the state health service (ISS).
SM.medical: Law 113/2021: medical cannabis on doctor's prescription, dispensed only by State pharmacies (ISS pharmaceutical service wholesale); licensed domestic cultivation framework

SN.name: Senegal
SN.headline: Illegal; users face jail, traffickers face long sentences
SN.law: Drug Code (Law 97-18, 1997), toughened by Law 2007-31: cultivation, possession, use and sale of cannabis ('chanvre indien') are crimes. No medical or hemp exception.
SN.punishment: Personal-use possession: 2 months-1 year plus fine of 3x drug value (Art. 109). Trafficking: multi-year prison; 2007 law sets heavy terms (10+ years) for large-scale/international trafficking.
SN.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
SN.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

SO.name: Somalia
SO.headline: Illegal everywhere; very harsh in al-Shabaab areas
SO.law: Cannabis is illegal under Somali law (1962 Penal Code, applied alongside Islamic law) and the separate laws of Somaliland and Puntland. Khat is legal and widely used; cannabis is not.
SO.punishment: Prison and fines under state law; exact ranges not verified. In al-Shabaab-held areas, militant 'courts' impose floggings and other extrajudicial punishments. Not on HRI's list of drug death-penalty states.
SO.access: No legal access. No medical program.
SO.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.
SO.subnational: Somaliland and Puntland apply their own laws; al-Shabaab areas apply militant punishments.

SR.name: Suriname
SR.headline: Illegal for all uses despite Dutch ties; no medical program
SR.law: Cannabis is banned under Suriname's narcotics law (Opiumwet). Possession, cultivation and sale are criminal; there is no decriminalization and no medical program. A 2022 industrial-hemp law (under 1% THC) is reported but its implementation is unclear.
SR.punishment: Possession: criminal offence with fines and/or prison; small amounts tend to draw lighter sentences. Trafficking and cultivation: multi-year prison terms. Exact statutory ranges not verified.
SR.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis program.

SS.name: South Sudan
SS.headline: Illegal; jail for use or dealing, but the death penalty excludes cannabis
SS.law: Penal Code Act 2008 (ss.383-384) makes possessing, using, growing or dealing cannabis ('dangerous drug') a crime. The aggravated dealing offence carrying death applies only to drugs OTHER than cannabis.
SS.punishment: Possession, use or growing for own use: up to 5 years and/or a fine (s.384). Dealing: up to 14 years and/or a fine (s.383). The death/life tier explicitly excludes cannabis.
SS.access: No legal access. No medical program.
SS.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.
SS.death_detail: Death/life applies to aggravated dealing in drugs other than cannabis; s.383(3) Penal Code 2008 excludes cannabis.

ST.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
ST.headline: Illegal; drug use and trafficking are criminal
ST.law: Cannabis is prohibited under national drug law. Cultivation, possession, use and sale are offences. No medical or hemp program.
ST.punishment: Use/possession: penalties apply (prison and/or fines). Trafficking: prison terms. Exact current ranges not verified.
ST.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
ST.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

SV.name: El Salvador
SV.headline: Illegal and strictly enforced; any amount is a crime
SV.law: Ley Reguladora de las Actividades Relativas a las Drogas bans possession, cultivation and sale. Art. 34 criminalizes possession of even small amounts; there is no personal-use exemption. Enforcement is harsh under the ongoing state of exception.
SV.punishment: Possession under 2 g: 1-3 years prison plus fine; 2 g or more: 3-6 years; possession with intent to traffic: 6-10 years. Trafficking (Art. 33): 10-15 years.
SV.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis program.
SV.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal penalties.

SY.name: Syria
SY.headline: Illegal; the law allows death for trafficking, but no death sentence for marijuana is documented
SY.law: All use, possession, cultivation and trade banned under the Narcotics Law (Law 2 of 1993). The post-Assad authorities (since Dec 2024) have kept the ban and are focused on fighting the captagon trade.
SY.punishment: Personal use: prison (Law 2/1993 sets years-long terms) plus fines. Trafficking: 10 years to life; smuggling, manufacture or cultivation of cannabis carry death (reducible to life/20+ yrs if mitigating).
SY.tourists: No. Visitors face the same penalties.
SY.death_detail: Death for smuggling or manufacturing narcotics incl. cannabis, and for cultivating cannabis (Table 4), under Law 2/1993 art.39(a); death for aggravated trafficking (art.40(b)). Kept in force by the post-Assad authorities; HRI: insufficient data on use.

SZ.name: Eswatini
SZ.headline: Illegal; medical cannabis bill still pending
SZ.law: The Opium and Habit-Forming Drugs Act 1922 bans cannabis. The Health Minister may license medical or research use (one firm is reported licensed). A medical cannabis and hemp bill has circulated since 2020 but has not been enacted.
SZ.punishment: Possession and trafficking are crimes under the 1922 Act (fines and prison); exact ranges not verified.
SZ.access: No legal access for individuals. Only ministerial licences under the 1922 Act exist; there is no patient program.
SZ.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.
SZ.medical: Ministerial licences only; medical bill pending

TD.name: Chad
TD.headline: Illegal; use and trafficking are criminal
TD.law: Cannabis is prohibited under Chad's Penal Code (2017) and drug-control provisions. Cultivation, possession, use and sale are crimes. No medical program. Chad abolished the death penalty in 2020.
TD.punishment: Use/possession: prison and fines. Trafficking: long prison terms. Exact current ranges not verified.
TD.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
TD.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

TG.name: Togo
TG.headline: Illegal; drug offences carry up to 20 years
TG.law: Cannabis use, possession, transport, resale and trafficking are crimes under the Penal Code (Law 2015-010, amended 2022) and drug-control law. No medical or hemp program.
TG.punishment: Small quantity for personal use: 1-6 months and/or 25,000-500,000 CFA (cannabis oil: 2 months-1 year, 25,000-1,250,000 CFA); a first-time adult can be excused if they pledge in court not to reoffend (Law 98-008 art. 112). Cultivation, sale, transport, possession (trafficking): 10-20 years and/or 250,000-125,000,000 CFA (arts. 98-99). Giving/offering for personal use: 3-5 years.
TG.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis or hemp licensing program.
TG.tourists: No. Use and possession are criminal for everyone.

TH.name: Thailand
TH.headline: Medical only since June 2025: flower needs a doctor's prescription
TH.law: Delisted as a narcotic in June 2022 (recreational boom). June 2025 order made flower a 'controlled herb': sale only on medical prescription; recreational use no longer lawful. Extracts >0.2% THC stay narcotics. Cabinet approved a medical-only Cannabis Act draft 22 Sep 2026.
TH.punishment: Not a narcotics crime: unlicensed sale/sale without prescription brings fines, licence loss and possible jail; public smoking fine up to ฿25,000. Extracts >0.2% THC and smuggling are narcotics offences (prison). Tougher penalties proposed Oct 2026.
TH.access: Licensed shops may sell flower only with a PT33 prescription (about 30 days' supply) from a licensed practitioner, often on site; over 7,000 shops closed. Government says further tightening coming.
TH.tourists: Only with a Thai PT33 prescription (passport needed). Foreign prescriptions invalid.
TH.possession_limit: Only the amount on a valid prescription
TH.home_grow: Unclear: notification/permit regime; unlicensed grow risky
TH.medical: Yes: national medical system; PT33 prescription required for flower since 2025.
TH.death_detail: Drug death penalty covers Category 1 drugs (heroin, meth), not cannabis.

TJ.name: Tajikistan
TJ.headline: Strictly illegal; long sentences on the Afghan trafficking route
TJ.law: Criminal Code bans possession, cultivation and trafficking of cannabis. The death penalty remains in law for some crimes (under moratorium since 2004) but not for drug offences.
TJ.punishment: Possession: fines or prison, by quantity. Trafficking: long prison terms (up to about 15-20 yrs) for large amounts.

TL.name: Timor-Leste
TL.headline: Illegal; personal use is a minor crime, trafficking 5–15 years
TL.law: Law 2/2017 on drug trafficking and consumption lists cannabis in Table I-C. Use and possession for personal use are crimes but lightly punished; occasional users may be exempted. President has urged treating cannabis apart from hard drugs.
TL.punishment: Personal use/possession: up to 6 months or fine (over 5 days' supply: up to 1 yr). Trafficking: 5–15 yrs (minor cases 1–5 yrs); aggravated: 10–25 yrs.
TL.access: No legal access. No medical program.
TL.tourists: No. Same law applies to visitors.

TM.name: Turkmenistan
TM.headline: Strictly illegal; among the harshest drug regimes in the region
TM.law: Criminal Code bans possession, cultivation and trafficking of all narcotics incl. cannabis. Enforcement is strict and opaque.
TM.punishment: Possession: prison terms of several years are common. Trafficking: long prison terms (up to about 15-25 yrs) and asset confiscation.

TN.name: Tunisia
TN.headline: Illegal; jail for use, reform bill pending
TN.law: Use, possession and trade banned under Law 52 of 1992. A 2017 amendment let judges apply leniency to first-time users; bill 11/2025 to ease use penalties was still in committee in 2026.
TN.punishment: Personal use: 1-5 years' prison plus fine (first offenders may get reduced/suspended terms). Trafficking: 6-10 years, up to life for organised/international.
TN.tourists: No. Visitors face the same penalties.

TO.name: Tonga
TO.headline: Illegal; no medical cannabis, strict drug law
TO.law: Cannabis is prohibited under the Illicit Drugs Control Act 2003 (toughened in 2020). Possession, cultivation and sale are crimes. 2019 medical cannabis lobbying was rejected by the Health Ministry; no hemp category exists.
TO.punishment: Possession: up to 5 yrs prison or T$10,000 fine (reported). Dealing/trafficking: much heavier, up to long or life terms with large fines (reported).
TO.access: No legal access. No medical program.

TR.name: Turkey
TR.headline: Illegal; personal use is a crime with 2-5 years' prison
TR.law: Use, possession, sale and unlicensed growing are crimes (Penal Code arts 188, 191; amended 2014). The state licenses hemp/cannabis farming in 19 provinces (2016 rules) for medical/industrial use only.
TR.punishment: Personal use/possession: 2-5 years' prison; first offenders usually get deferred prosecution with treatment/probation. Sale/supply: 10-20 years; production/import/export: 20-30 years.
TR.access: No legal access for consumers. Only state-licensed farms grow cannabis for industry and pharma.
TR.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal penalties.
TR.medical: No patient program; licensed farming for medical/industrial use only

TT.name: Trinidad and Tobago
TT.headline: Up to 30 g and 4 plants allowed for adults; no legal sales
TT.law: Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act 2019 (in force Dec 2019): adults may possess up to 30 g (5 g resin) and grow 4 plants with no penalty. Public smoking and all sale remain illegal. Cannabis Control Bill for licensing still not in force.
TT.punishment: Up to 30 g: no penalty. 30–60 g: fixed-penalty ticket (reported TT$2,000). 60–100 g: up to TT$75,000 fine and community service. Trafficking: criminal, long prison terms.
TT.access: Home grow only (4 plants per adult). No licensed shops or medical program.
TT.tourists: Possession up to 30 g is not penalised, but there is no legal place to buy.
TT.medical: No operating program; Cannabis Control Bill pending

TV.name: Tuvalu
TV.headline: Illegal; no legal or medical access
TV.law: Cannabis is prohibited under Tuvalu's dangerous/narcotic drugs legislation; possession, cultivation and sale are criminal offences. Drug crime is rare.
TV.punishment: Possession and supply are criminal offences carrying prison and/or fines; exact current maximums not confirmed.
TV.access: No legal access. No medical program.

TW.name: Taiwan
TW.headline: Illegal Category 2 narcotic; trafficking up to life (death only for officials abusing office)
TW.law: Cannabis is a Category 2 narcotic under the Narcotics Hazard Prevention Act. Use, possession, cultivation and sale are all criminal. First-time users are often diverted to treatment/deferred prosecution.
TW.punishment: Use: up to 3 yrs. Possession: up to 2 yrs or fine NT$200,000 (>20 g pure: 6 mo–5 yrs). Manufacture/transport/sale: life or ≥10 yrs + fine up to NT$15 million.
TW.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis program.
TW.tourists: No. Visitors face the same penalties; importing cannabis is trafficking.
TW.death_detail: Death applies to Category 1 drugs. Cannabis is Category 2 (max life), BUT civil servants who abuse their office to make, transport or sell it face death or life (art.15).

TZ.name: Tanzania
TZ.headline: Illegal; very long sentences, even for small amounts
TZ.law: Drug Control and Enforcement Act 2015 (Cap. 95, revised 2023) bans growing, possessing, using or selling cannabis (bangi). A 2026 amendment bill would also criminalise possessing seeds of prohibited plants.
TZ.punishment: Severe and rising: a court gave a 30-year sentence for 90 g of cannabis in 2026. Trafficking or cultivation: 30 years to life (reported). Small amounts may draw fines.
TZ.access: No legal access. No medical program.
TZ.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.
TZ.subnational: Zanzibar has its own drug control law; it is also strict.

UA.name: Ukraine
UA.headline: Medical cannabis law 2024; first pharmacy sales June 2026; recreational illegal
UA.law: Law 3528-IX (in force 16 Aug 2024) allows cannabis medicines on e-prescription; first products registered Jan 2025, first dispensing 11 Jun 2026. Up to 5 g possession is an administrative offence; more is criminal. Sale illegal.
UA.punishment: Up to 5 g: fine, community service or up to 15 days admin arrest. Above: up to 3 yrs (large 2-5 yrs). Trafficking: 4-8 yrs; up to 12 yrs for especially large amounts.
UA.access: Medical only: e-prescription (valid 10 days) for listed conditions (chronic pain, cancer, MS, epilepsy etc.), filled at a few licensed pharmacies. No shops or home grow.
UA.medical: Yes: law 2024, pharmacy dispensing since June 2026, e-prescription
UA.subnational: Russian-occupied areas are under Russian law in practice.

UG.name: Uganda
UG.headline: Illegal for adults; licensed medical cultivation for export only
UG.law: The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Control) Act 2023 replaced the 2015 law, which the Constitutional Court annulled. Recreational use, possession and sale stay criminal. The Health Ministry can license medical cultivation.
UG.punishment: Possession: heavy fines and/or prison (reportedly up to 10 years). Trafficking: up to life imprisonment, plus forfeiture of assets.
UG.access: No legal access for individuals. A few licensed firms grow medical cannabis for export; there is no domestic dispensary or prescription route.
UG.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.
UG.medical: Licensed export cultivation only; no patient access

US.name: United States
US.headline: Federally illegal; legal in 24 states + DC; unused federal kingpin death law
US.law: Federal law (Controlled Substances Act) still bans adult use and sale. April 2026 rule moved only state-licensed medical and FDA-approved marijuana to Schedule III; broader rescheduling still pending at DEA. States set their own rules.
US.punishment: Federal: simple possession up to 1 yr + min $1,000 fine (first offence); trafficking up to 5 yrs (<50 kg), 5–40 yrs (100 kg+), 10 yrs–life (1,000 kg+). 18 USC 3591(b) allows death for kingpins (60,000 kg+); never applied, likely unconstitutional.
US.access: Depends on state: licensed dispensaries in most of the 24 adult-use states; medical cards in about 40 states. No federal legal access outside FDA-approved drugs.
US.tourists: Yes in adult-use states (21+, ID); federal land, airports and border crossings stay illegal.
US.home_grow: Varies by state (e.g. 6 plants); illegal federally
US.medical: State programs in about 40 states; state-licensed medical marijuana now federal Schedule III (2026)
US.death_detail: Federal law (18 USC 3591(b)(1) + 21 USC 848) allows death in theory for a continuing-criminal-enterprise leader dealing twice the 848(b) quantity, i.e. 60,000 kg or 60,000 plants of marijuana (or $20M gross receipts). Never used; constitutionality untested.
US.subnational: 24 states + DC allow adult use (e.g. CA, CO, NY, IL, OH); about 40 allow medical; the rest prohibit. Local police enforce state law.

UY.name: Uruguay
UY.headline: Fully legal for registered residents: pharmacies, home grow or clubs
UY.law: Law 19.172 (2013) legalized adult cannabis under state control (IRCCA). Pharmacy sales began July 2017. Adults must register for one route: pharmacy, home grow, or club. Only citizens and legal residents may register.
UY.punishment: Unregistered possession above personal amounts or sale outside the system is prosecuted. Trafficking (Law 14.294): 20 months to 10 years prison.
UY.access: Easy for residents: 4 strains (up to 20% THC) at about 24 pharmacies, 10 g/week, 40 g/month; home grow 6 plants; clubs of 15-45 members. 83,567 pharmacy buyers in 2025.
UY.tourists: No. Non-residents cannot register or buy; IRCCA only discussing it (Dec 2025).

UZ.name: Uzbekistan
UZ.headline: Strictly illegal; long prison terms for trafficking
UZ.law: Criminal Code bans possession, cultivation and sale of cannabis (art. 276 possession without intent to sell; art. 273 trafficking). Small amounts may be handled administratively for first offences.
UZ.punishment: Possession without intent to sell: a fine, or up to about 3 years in prison. Trafficking ('transfer', incl. gifting/dead-drops): multi-year terms; 7-10 yrs if online or near schools, 15-20 yrs for large quantities (Law LRU-1151, 11 Jun 2026); no parole for large-quantity offences. Public drug use: up to 15 days' administrative detention.

VA.name: Vatican City
VA.headline: Illegal; no medical program
VA.law: Narcotics, including cannabis, are prohibited; Vatican criminal law is based on Italian-derived codes. No decriminalisation and no medical program. Offences on Vatican territory may be handled with Italian authorities.
VA.punishment: Possession and trafficking are criminal offences; specific penalty ranges are not publicly documented.

VC.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
VC.headline: Up to 2 oz is a ticket; licensed medical cannabis industry
VC.law: Misuse of Drugs (Amendment) Act 2018 made up to 2 oz (56 g) a ticketable offence with no criminal record; use at home and in Rastafari places of worship not punished. Medicinal Cannabis Industry Act 2018 licenses medical cultivation and supply.
VC.punishment: Up to 2 oz: fine up to EC$500 plus counselling, no record. Larger amounts and trafficking: criminal; e.g. 2024 case with 13.6 kg drew EC$9,000 fines; prison possible.
VC.access: Moderate: medical cannabis via prescription from licensed dispensaries under the Medicinal Cannabis Authority. No recreational shops.
VC.tourists: No recreational purchase; medical only with prescription.
VC.medical: Licensed industry under Medicinal Cannabis Authority since 2018

VE.name: Venezuela
VE.headline: Illegal; up to 20 g for personal use brings treatment, not prison
VE.law: Ley Orgánica de Drogas (2010) bans possession, cultivation and sale. Possession up to 20 g, if shown to be for personal use, leads to court-ordered security measures (rehab/detox) instead of prison. No medical program.
VE.punishment: Up to 20 g personal: treatment measures; if not personal use, 1-2 years prison. Trafficking: about 8-12 years for small quantities, 15-25 years for larger amounts.
VE.access: No legal access. No medical cannabis program.
VE.tourists: No. Non-resident foreigners can also be expelled.
VE.possession_limit: 20 g (treated as personal use, still unlawful)

VN.name: Vietnam
VN.headline: Illegal; big trafficking cases can carry death
VN.law: Cannabis is banned under the 2015 Penal Code and 2021 Law on Drug Prevention. Use is mainly an administrative offence (rehab for addicts) but became a crime for some relapsing users in 2025 (Art. 256a); possession above thresholds and any sale are crimes. July 2025 reform (Law 86/2025) ended death for drug transport and raised the death thresholds for trafficking.
VN.punishment: Use: fines/compulsory rehab; since 1 July 2025 use during or soon after rehab/post-rehab management is a crime (Art. 256a: 2–3 yrs, repeat 3–5 yrs). Possession ≥1 kg leaf/flower or ≥1 g resin: 3–5 yrs, more for larger amounts. Sale: 3–7 yrs base; resin 5–<30 kg or leaf/flower 75–<150 kg: 20 yrs or life; resin ≥30 kg or leaf/flower ≥150 kg: life or death (Art. 251(5)).
VN.access: No legal access. No medical program.
VN.tourists: No. Foreigners have been sentenced to death for drug trafficking.
VN.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: 12 Jun 2026: Quang Ninh Provincial People's Court (first instance) sentenced Nguyen Phi Co and Nguyen Duy Manh to death in a 401 kg cannabis (can sa) Telegram trafficking ring. Also 2010: 5 Chinese men sentenced to death for about 8 t cannabis resin. Note: 2026 proposal to abolish death for drug trafficking pending. Art. 251(5) (as amended 1 Jul 2025): selling cannabis resin ≥30 kg or leaf/flower ≥150 kg → life or death. Pre-July-2025 death sentences below the new thresholds are commuted. 85+ drug death sentences in 2025; executions secret (HRI).

VU.name: Vanuatu
VU.headline: Illegal for all personal use; 2021 law licenses export-only medical cannabis/hemp farming (not yet operating)
VU.law: Recreational use, possession and sale are illegal. The Industrial Hemp and Medical Cannabis Act No. 31 of 2021 (regulations 2023) lets a few licensed firms grow medical cannabis and hemp, mainly for export. No personal use rights.
VU.punishment: Possession, cultivation and supply outside a licence are offences under the Dangerous Drugs Act; prison terms and large fines possible (reported maximum up to 20 yrs and/or heavy fines).
VU.access: Practically none for individuals: licences go to companies (cultivation/export), and banking problems stalled the industry. No clear domestic patient prescription route.
VU.tourists: No. Recreational use illegal for everyone.
VU.medical: Export-only production licensing (2021 Act); no local sales or patient program

WS.name: Samoa
WS.headline: Illegal; jail sentences common even for small amounts
WS.law: Cannabis is a narcotic under the Narcotics Act 1967; possession, cultivation, import and supply are criminal offences. No medical program.
WS.punishment: Possession or cultivation: up to 14 yrs prison; small amounts get community service to about 2 yrs jail in recent cases. Supply/dealing prosecuted more severely.
WS.access: No legal access. No medical program.
WS.tourists: No. Illegal for everyone; border seizures prosecuted.

XK.name: Kosovo
XK.headline: Illegal for all uses; first-time small possession usually a fine
XK.law: Criminal Code bans possession, cultivation and sale of cannabis. No medical program. Industrial hemp legal; CBD in a grey area.
XK.punishment: Small personal possession: fine (about EUR 250-300) or up to 1 yr; larger amounts 1-3 yrs. Cultivation/trafficking: 1-10 yrs.
XK.access: No legal access. No medical program.

YE.name: Yemen
YE.headline: Illegal; trafficking can carry death, sentences handed down yearly
YE.law: All use, possession and trade banned under Law No. 3 of 1993 on narcotics. Applied by both the government and Houthi courts.
YE.punishment: Personal use: prison (years) plus fines. Trafficking: death or long prison. 17+ drug death sentences in 2025; 30+ people on drug death row (HRI).
YE.tourists: No. Visitors face the same penalties.
YE.death_detail: Death sentence given for marijuana: 2009: Hadramout court sentenced 7 to death for bringing 2.4 t hashish by sea; 2011 two Pakistanis for 1,600 kg hashish; Oct 2025 six Iranians for about 3 t hashish + crystal meth. Death for trafficking/smuggling (Law 3/1993). 17+ drug death sentences in 2025, many for hashish smuggling (HRI).
YE.subnational: Houthi-run north and government-held south both enforce the 1993 law; Houthi courts issue most death sentences.

ZA.name: South Africa
ZA.headline: Legal for adults in private; buying and selling remain illegal
ZA.law: The Constitutional Court's 2018 Prince ruling legalised adult private use, possession and growing. The Cannabis for Private Purposes Act (2024) is signed but not yet in force; draft regulations were published in Feb 2026.
ZA.punishment: Private adult use: no offence. Dealing or selling: up to 25 years under the Drugs and Drug Trafficking Act 1992. Use in public and supplying minors are also offences.
ZA.access: Grow your own at home or receive it as a gift. Commercial 'dagga clubs' and shops are not legal. Medical products are available via SAHPRA authorisation or prescription.
ZA.tourists: Private use only; no legal place to buy.
ZA.home_grow: Legal in private (draft regulations: 5 plants per adult)

ZM.name: Zambia
ZM.headline: Illegal for adults; 2021 law licenses medical cannabis and hemp
ZM.law: The Cannabis Act 2021 (No. 33) licenses medicinal and research cultivation and production; the Industrial Hemp Act 2021 (No. 34) covers hemp. Recreational use stays illegal under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act.
ZM.punishment: Recreational possession and trafficking carry long prison terms; exact ranges not verified (reports cite up to 10-25 years).
ZM.access: No personal access. A licensing framework exists, but commercial licences have been slow to issue.
ZM.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.
ZM.medical: Cannabis Act 2021 framework; operational licensing slow

ZW.name: Zimbabwe
ZW.headline: Illegal for adults; licensed medical cannabis farming since 2018
ZW.law: SI 62 of 2018 licenses cannabis production for medical and scientific use (hemp was added in 2019). Recreational possession, use and sale stay criminal under the Dangerous Drugs Act and the Criminal Law Code.
ZW.punishment: Possession: fine and/or prison. Dealing: long prison terms (historically up to about 12-15 years reported); exact current ranges not verified.
ZW.access: No personal access. Licensed producers only (fees of about US$15,000+), mainly for export; no domestic dispensaries.
ZW.tourists: No. Visitors face the same criminal law.
